Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Eight

section: Romans 9:6 — The Premise Regarding Israel: True Israel and the Validity of the Word of God
text: Romans 9:6 — The Premise Regarding Israel: True Israel and the Validity of the Word of God

section: Romans 9:6 — The Premise Regarding Israel: True Israel and the Validity of the Word of God
text: Romans 9:6 “But it is not as though the word of God has failed. For not all who are descended from Israel belong to Israel.” (ESV)

section: Romans 9:6 — The Premise Regarding Israel: True Israel and the Validity of the Word of God
text: Corrected translation: However, this is not to imply that the Word of God has failed, for not all who are descended from Israel are really Israel.

section: Romans 9:6 — The Premise Regarding Israel: True Israel and the Validity of the Word of God
text: Romans 9:6 opens the second major division of chapter 9, the premise regarding Israel. Paul has just declared his personal burden for the Jewish people and catalogued their extraordinary spiritual heritage — the adoption, the Shekinah glory, the unconditional covenants, the Mosaic law, the worship of the true God, and the promises. He has identified the regenerate ancestors — Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob — and affirmed that from their line came the Christ, who is God over all, praised forever. Now, before moving to the exposition of those covenants, Paul addresses the urgent pastoral question: Has the Word of God been nullified? He answers in a single verse of concentrated exegetical and theological force, drawing on the resources of classical Greek idiom to make his point.

section: I. The Classical Greek Idiom of Romans 9:6a
text: I. The Classical Greek Idiom of Romans 9:6a

section: I. The Classical Greek Idiom of Romans 9:6a
text: The verse does not begin where most English translations suggest. The Greek opens with the post-positive conjunctive particle

section: I. The Classical Greek Idiom of Romans 9:6a
text: The verse does not begin where most English translations suggest. The Greek opens with the post-positive conjunctive particle de (δέ), translated but, which signals contrast with what has immediately preceded. To that is joined the strong negative ou (οὐ), yielding the idiom ouch hoios (οὐχ οἷος). The word hoios (οἷος) is a derivative correlative pronoun used in classical Attic Greek — the dialect of Athens and of the great dramatists — as part of an elliptical idiom. Euripides employed it in precisely this way: the pronoun appears in the predicate nominative without a stated verb, requiring the reader to supply the present indicative of eimi (εἰμί), the verb to be. This is not an addition to the text; it is a grammatical necessity. When a nominative subject is followed by a predicate nominative and no verb is present, Koine Greek syntax requires the insertion of the implied copula. The idiom as a whole means: not such as, not of that kind, not as implying.

section: I. The Classical Greek Idiom of Romans 9:6a
text: The idiom is then concluded by the conjunction

section: I. The Classical Greek Idiom of Romans 9:6a
text: The idiom is then concluded by the conjunction hoti (ὅτι), which resumes the discourse and introduces the content of what is being negated. Together the construction reads: However, this is not to imply that. What is lost in any English rendering is the elegance of the construction itself. Paul has brought his readers to the edge of a great theological precipice using one of the most beautiful idioms in all of classical Greek, and before they can exhale, he drops the substantive point. The effect is deliberate and unmistakable: the reader is arrested, drawn in, and then confronted with the premise.

section: II. The Verb: ekpiptō and the Alleged Failure of the Word
text: II. The Verb: ekpiptō and the Alleged Failure of the Word

section: II. The Verb: ekpiptō and the Alleged Failure of the Word
text: The noun subject of the clause is ho logos (ὁ λόγος) with the possessive genitive singular tou theou (τοῦ θεοῦ). The definite article carries a generic force, denoting the absolute uniqueness of the canon of Scripture. Logos means more than word in the simple sense; it encompasses the thought that words convey, the ordered communication of meaning. The phrase is therefore rendered: the Word of God.

section: II. The Verb: ekpiptō and the Alleged Failure of the Word
text: The verb is the perfect active indicative of the compound verb ekpiptō (ἐκπίπτω), from ek (out of, from) + piptō (to fall). The compound means to fall from, to fall off, and in extended use to fail, to lose force and validity. It was a nautical term: to drift off course or to run aground. Here it means to become void, to be annulled, to fail of its purpose.

section: II. The Verb: ekpiptō and the Alleged Failure of the Word
text: The perfect tense is consummative, presenting the past process and its present apparent result. The active voice presents the Word of God as the alleged subject of the failure — alleged, because this is precisely what Paul is denying. The indicative mood is potential: it presents the allegation as a real claim in the minds of contemporary Jewish readers, but the context makes clear that this alleged failure has no actual foundation. The indicative is not asserting the failure; it is identifying and then refuting the allegation.

section: II. The Verb: ekpiptō and the Alleged Failure of the Word
text: The situation Paul addresses is this: the majority of Jews in his day had concluded, on the basis of Israel's discipline and the insertion of the Church Age, that God had abandoned His promises to the nation. The times of the Gentiles — the period during which Israel no longer functions as the client nation to God — appeared to them as evidence that the Old Testament covenants had been abrogated. The unconditional covenants given to Abraham, amplified through Moses and the prophets, elaborated especially in Isaiah, pointed to a glorious national and eternal future for Israel. Yet here was the Church Age, the administration of the fifth cycle of discipline, the destruction of Jerusalem in AD 70, and Israel scattered and without a functioning theocratic structure. The conclusion many drew was: the Word of God has failed.

section: II. The Verb: ekpiptō and the Alleged Failure of the Word
text: Paul's answer is not to retreat from the promises, but to redefine the subject of those promises. The Word of God has not failed. What has been misunderstood is who constitutes the true Israel to whom those promises were made.

section: III. The Second Clause: For Not All Who Are Descended from Israel Are Really Israel
text: III. The Second Clause: For Not All Who Are Descended from Israel Are Really Israel

section: III. The Second Clause: For Not All Who Are Descended from Israel Are Really Israel
text: The second clause begins with the explanatory use of the conjunctive particle gar (γάρ), for, introducing the ground or explanation of the preceding denial. Then comes the objective negative adverb ou (οὐ), which denies the reality of an alleged fact. The alleged fact is this: possession of the genes of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob constitutes automatic membership in the true Israel and automatic claim on the promises of God.

section: III. The Second Clause: For Not All Who Are Descended from Israel Are Really Israel
text: The nominative masculine plural subject pantes (πάντες) means all, referring to racial Jews — those who possess the genetic descent from Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. The nominative plural definite article hoi (οἱ) is used as a relative pronoun with pantes as its antecedent, introducing a relative clause: who are descended from. The prepositional phrase ex Israel (ἐξ Ἰσραήλ) uses the preposition ek (ἐκ) with the indeclinable proper noun Israel (Ἰσραήλ), meaning descended from Israel.

section: III. The Second Clause: For Not All Who Are Descended from Israel Are Really Israel
text: The predicate is the demonstrative pronoun houtoi (οὗτοι) in the nominative masculine plural. The demonstrative force of houtoi — these, these very ones — emphasizes the true Israel: all born-again believers in Christ, the spiritual seed rather than the physical seed. This pronoun supplies the predicate nominative, requiring the implicit copula: are really Israel. The second occurrence of Israel refers to the true, regenerate Israel composed of believers.

section: III. The Second Clause: For Not All Who Are Descended from Israel Are Really Israel
text: The corrected translation of the full verse is therefore: However, this is not to imply that the Word of God has failed, for not all who are descended from Israel are really Israel.

section: IV. The Distinction Between Racial and Regenerate Israel
text: IV. The Distinction Between Racial and Regenerate Israel

section: IV. The Distinction Between Racial and Regenerate Israel
text: The verse introduces and requires a sustained distinction between two categories of Jewishness: the racial Jew and the regenerate Jew. Paul is not abolishing the significance of physical descent; he is insisting that physical descent is insufficient as the basis for the promises of God. This distinction must be traced carefully.

section: A. Origin in the Radical Framework
text: A. Origin in the Radical Framework

section: A. Origin in the Radical Framework
text: All human beings, Jew and Gentile alike, begin at birth in what may be called the first category of the divine plan — the condition of physical life without spiritual life, the point at which human life is imputed to the soul at birth while Adam's original sin is simultaneously imputed to the genetically formed old sin nature. All Gentiles trace their descent through Noah's sons — Shem, Ham, and Japheth — all of whom were believers, but whose physical descent transmits no spiritual standing to their posterity.

section: A. Origin in the Radical Framework
text: The Jewish race is unique in its origin. Abraham, descended from Noah through Shem, was a Gentile by birth. He became a Jew — the first Jew — not through physical birth but through his mature faith and his circumcision, which was the outward sign of his maturity adjustment to the justice of God. Abraham at approximately one hundred years of age had achieved two spiritual realities: salvation adjustment to the justice of God through faith in Christ, and maturity adjustment to the justice of God through maximum doctrine resident in the soul. These two adjustments define the origination of the Jewish race in a condition of maximum blessing.

section: A. Origin in the Radical Framework
text: The critical point is this: every son born to Abraham after that point — Isaac included — was born physically into the same condition as every other human being. The genes of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob are transmitted by physical birth; the spiritual standing of Abraham is not. A Jewish child is born with no more spiritual standing than a Gentile child. Both begin at the same starting point, under condemnation, without imputed righteousness, without eternal life. The Jewish advantage lies not in birth but in the heritage of the promises — and those promises are conditional upon the same response that Abraham himself made: faith in the Lord Jesus Christ.

section: B. The Error of Terminal Self-Righteousness
text: B. The Error of Terminal Self-Righteousness

section: B. The Error of Terminal Self-Righteousness
text: The majority of Jews in Paul's day had made a fatal assumption. They had concluded that possession of the genes of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob placed them automatically in the category of God's covenant people — that birth into the Jewish race was equivalent to standing in the relationship of blessing that Abraham achieved through faith and maturity. In theological terms, they had transplanted themselves from the condition of unbelief into the category of covenant blessing without passing through the two adjustments that define that category.

section: B. The Error of Terminal Self-Righteousness
text: This is what Paul calls, by implication, terminal self-righteousness. The Mosaic law had been misapplied as the means of righteousness before God, displacing faith in Christ. The result was a collective and individual rejection of the Shekinah glory — the Lord Jesus Christ — when He appeared in the flesh. The Jews had the Shekinah glory in the holy of holies, present but invisible. At the first advent, the Shekinah glory became visible: He tabernacled among them, they heard Him, they observed His miracles. And they rejected Him. This rejection constituted the great collective failure of Israel and led directly to the fifth cycle of discipline culminating in AD 70.

section: C. True Israel: The Regenerate Jew
text: C. True Israel: The Regenerate Jew

section: C. True Israel: The Regenerate Jew
text: The true Israel, then, is the born-again Jew. He possesses the genes of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob — he is racially a Jew, the physical seed of Abraham — but he does not become the true Jew, the spiritual seed of Abraham, until he believes in the Lord Jesus Christ as Savior. That is the salvation adjustment to the justice of God. From that point, through continued daily intake of Bible doctrine, he advances toward maturity — the maturity adjustment to the justice of God — and it is at maturity that he fulfills the pattern of Abraham himself, who became a Jew at the moment of his circumcision, the sign of his spiritual maturity.

section: C. True Israel: The Regenerate Jew
text: This is the force of Jesus's statement to Nicodemus, the ruler of the Jews: you must be born again. The new birth is not a message incidental to Jewishness — it is the essential condition of true Jewishness. Without it, the racial Jew has no claim on the Abrahamic, Palestinian, Davidic, or New Covenants to Israel. Those covenants were made with Abraham as a mature believer, not with Abraham as a racial ancestor. They belong to his spiritual seed, not his physical seed alone.

section: V. Principles Emerging from Romans 9:6
text: V. Principles Emerging from Romans 9:6

section: V. Principles Emerging from Romans 9:6
text: The following principles emerge from the exegesis of this verse and the doctrinal framework it establishes.

section: A. On the Word of God and the Plan of God
text: A. On the Word of God and the Plan of God

section: A. On the Word of God and the Plan of God
text: Individual and collective failure does not hinder the plan of God or the validity of the Word of God. The plan of God moves on with or without the participation of any individual or nation. God does not need any person or nation to fulfill His purposes; every person and nation needs God. The failure of contemporary Israel — whether the rejection of Christ by the majority or the administration of the fifth cycle of discipline — does not cancel anything in the Word of God. The promises remain valid because the God who made them is immutable. Human rejection of Christ does not imply the failure of the Word of God; it implies only that the individual has failed to use his free will and self-determination to believe in Christ. The Word of God has not failed the Jew; the Jew has failed the Word of God.

section: B. On the Promises to Israel
text: B. On the Promises to Israel

section: B. On the Promises to Israel
text: The promises of God contained in the unconditional covenants to Israel — Abrahamic, Palestinian, Davidic, New — do not apply to racial Jews who have rejected Christ as Savior. They apply exclusively to true Israel, the born-again Jew. The alternative to blessing in the Word of God is judgment, and that alternative is as clearly stated in Scripture as the promises of grace. That many Jews are under divine judgment in every generation does not cancel the promises; it confirms them, for the Word of God promised judgment to those who reject the God of Israel in every generation.

section: B. On the Promises to Israel
text: God's promises have not become invalid through the exclusion of unbelieving Jews. The promises were never addressed to the racial Jew as such, but to the spiritual seed of Abraham — those who believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, the second person of the Trinity, revealed in the Old Testament as Jehovah Elohim, Adonai, the Shekinah glory, and in the New Testament as the Lord Jesus Christ. The name differs across languages and dispensations; the person is identical. Abraham believed in Adonai, and it was credited to him as righteousness — this is equivalent to saying he believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, for it is the same second person of the Trinity.

section: C. On the Plan of God for Jew and Gentile in the Same Condition
text: C. On the Plan of God for Jew and Gentile in the Same Condition

section: C. On the Plan of God for Jew and Gentile in the Same Condition
text: God's plan for the racial Jew who has not believed in Christ is identical to God's plan for the Gentile: salvation adjustment to the justice of God through faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. First John 3:23 states this as the will of God for all to whom human life has been imputed at birth: that they believe on the name of His Son Jesus Christ. This is equally the will of God for Jew and Gentile. Until the racial Jew has believed in Christ, his spiritual condition is no better than that of any Gentile, and may in fact be worse, because the greater the privilege, the greater the accountability. The only issue in the unbelieving condition is: what does he think of Christ?

section: C. On the Plan of God for Jew and Gentile in the Same Condition
text: Anti-Semitism — any human addition to the discipline God administers to the unbelieving Jew — constitutes an intrusion upon the prerogative of the justice of God and brings corresponding judgment upon the nation or individual that practices it. God administers His own justice without assistance. The nation that adds its curse to the Jew's discipline receives the consequences of both. This is the principle embedded in the Abrahamic Covenant itself: those who curse Israel will be cursed.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Eight
text: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Eight

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Eight
text: 1. Individual and collective failure does not hinder the plan of God nor the validity of the Word of God. The plan of God and the Word of God move on regardless of human failure, whether of individuals or of nations. God does not require human cooperation to fulfill His purposes.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Eight
text: 2. The plan of God and the Word of God move on with or without us. God does not need us; we need Him. Relegating Bible doctrine to a secondary place in life means falling behind a plan that does not pause for anyone.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Eight
text: 3. Collective or individual failure of the Jew does not abrogate the promises of God for the regenerate Israel. The rejection of the Shekinah glory at the first advent and the subsequent fifth cycle of discipline do not cancel the unconditional covenants. Those covenants belong to the spiritual seed of Abraham.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Eight
text: 4. Human failure simply cannot hinder the advance of the plan of God. Human plans collapse under human failure. The plan of God does not, because it rests on the immutability, omniscience, and omnipotence of the one who designed it.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Eight
text: 5. The failure of the unbeliever or believer does not imply the failure of the Word of God, which reveals the plan of God. The Word of God is the constant; human response is the variable. The Word does not fail because individuals reject it.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Eight
text: 6. Rejection of Jesus Christ, the God of Israel, places the Jew outside the plan of God and the unconditional covenants. The covenants were made with Abraham as a mature believer. They belong to his spiritual heirs, not to racial descent as such.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Eight
text: 7. Human rejection of Christ does not imply that the Word of God has failed, but that the Jew has failed to use his free will to believe in Christ. The failure is entirely in human volition. The Word of God stands unchanged.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Eight
text: 8. The alternative of divine judgment is as clearly presented in the Word of God as the blessings of grace. That many Jews are under divine judgment in every generation does not hinder the promises of God; it confirms that the Word of God is fulfilled on both sides — blessing to the believer, discipline to the unbeliever.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Eight
text: 9. The Word of God promises judgment in time and in eternity to the Jew who rejects the God of Israel. This has been true in every generation, Old Testament and New. The Jew who rejects Jehovah Elohim — the Lord Jesus Christ — faces the same justice as any Gentile who rejects Christ, but with greater accountability proportional to greater privilege.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Eight
text: 10. The Word of God has not failed the Jew; the Jew has failed the Word of God. The premise of Romans 9:6 reverses the allegation of the reversionistic Jew. The Word is not on trial; the response of the individual to the Word is.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Eight
text: 11. God's promises have not become untrue through the exclusion of unbelieving Jews. The promises can only be valid to one who possesses imputed righteousness and eternal life. These are received only through faith in Christ. Therefore God's promises are valid to the born-again Jew only.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Eight
text: 12. Scripture defines true and false Israel on the basis of attitude toward the Lord Jesus Christ. This has been the criterion in every dispensation. Jehovah, Adonai, Elohim in the Old Testament and the Lord Jesus Christ in the New Testament are one and the same second person of the Trinity. Abraham believed in Adonai, and it was credited to him as righteousness (Genesis 15:6, cited in Romans 4:3).

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Eight
text: 13. True Israel believes in the Lord God of Israel, Jesus Christ, following the pattern of Abraham. The promises of God are always valid to true Israel — those who believe in Christ and advance through doctrine to maturity.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Eight
text: 14. Having the genes of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob is not automatic salvation. All Jews are born into the same condition as all Gentiles — without imputed righteousness, without eternal life, under condemnation. Physical birth conveys the genetic heritage but no spiritual standing.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Eight
text: 15. The promises of God in the unconditional covenants to Israel do not apply to racial Jews who have rejected Christ as Savior. These covenants apply exclusively to the true Israel — the born-again Jew — who has received salvation adjustment to the justice of God through faith in Christ.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Eight
text: 16. Divine blessings to Israel, including salvation, do not come through the first birth but through the second birth. Physical birth places the Jew at the same starting point as every other human being. The new birth is the entry point into the covenant blessings.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Eight
text: 17. The real Jew is the born-again Jew. In physical birth, the Jew possesses the genes of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. In regeneration, the Jew possesses imputed righteousness, eternal life, and a future resurrection body. Only the regenerate Jew fulfills the true meaning of Israel.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Eight
text: 18. God's plan for the Jew in the condition of unbelief is identical to God's plan for the Gentile: faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. First John 3:23 states the will of God for all to whom human life has been imputed: that they believe on the name of His Son Jesus Christ. Nothing in the divine plan becomes operative for either Jew or Gentile until that first salvation adjustment.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Eight
text: 19. Anti-Semitism is an intrusion upon the prerogative of the justice of God and brings corresponding judgment. God administers His own discipline to Israel without human assistance. Any nation or individual that adds persecution to Israel's divinely administered discipline receives both the judgment due to that nation and the additional consequences of having intruded upon divine prerogative.

section: Romans 9:6–7 — The True Jew: Regeneration, Election, and the Seed of Abraham
text: Romans 9:6–7 — The True Jew: Regeneration, Election, and the Seed of Abraham

section: Romans 9:6–7 — The True Jew: Regeneration, Election, and the Seed of Abraham
text: Romans 9:6–7 “But it is not as though the word of God has failed. For not all who are descended from Israel belong to Israel, and not all are children of Abraham because they are his offspring, but 'Through Isaac shall your offspring be named.'” (ESV)

section: Romans 9:6–7 — The True Jew: Regeneration, Election, and the Seed of Abraham
text: Corrected translation: However, this is not to imply that the word of God has failed. For not all who are descended from Israel are really Israel; neither because they are Abraham's seed, posterity, are they all children of the inheritance. But in Isaac shall your seed be called.

section: Romans 9:6–7 — The True Jew: Regeneration, Election, and the Seed of Abraham
text: Romans 9 continues the apostle Paul's extended defense of the faithfulness of God toward Israel. Having established in verses 1–5 the extraordinary historical privileges of the Jewish race — the Shekinah glory, the unconditional covenants, the law, the worship, the patriarchs, and the Messiah himself — Paul now addresses the apparent problem: if Israel is so privileged, why does so much of Israel remain in unbelief and under divine judgment? His answer turns on a precise theological distinction: there are two Israels, a racial Israel and a true Israel, and the promises of God belong exclusively to the latter. This chapter examines the principles embedded in verse 6 and begins the first case history illustrating those principles — the sons of Abraham — in verse 7.

section: I. Principles Extrapolated from Romans 9:6
text: I. Principles Extrapolated from Romans 9:6

section: I. Principles Extrapolated from Romans 9:6
text: The declaration that the word of God has not failed rests upon a fundamental distinction between racial descent and spiritual identity. Verse 6b — 'for not all who are descended from Israel are really Israel' — is not a novelty introduced by Paul. It is the consistent witness of the Old Testament, now brought to its clearest New Testament expression. The following principles govern the interpretation of this verse and of the passage as a whole.

section: I. Principles Extrapolated from Romans 9:6
text: 1. God's plan for the Jew in the X-radical is the same as God's plan for the Gentile: freedom to hear the gospel, freedom to accept or reject it, with salvation adjustment to the justice of God available through faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. The Lord Jesus Christ is not only the Savior of mankind but the God of Israel — the Shekinah glory who appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Until a Jew believes in Christ, his spiritual condition is no better than that of any Gentile, whatever natural gifts or cultural heritage he may possess.

section: I. Principles Extrapolated from Romans 9:6
text: 2. The only issue in the X-radical is: what does one think of Christ? This issue applies equally to Jew and Gentile. As Paul stated in Romans 1:16, the gospel is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, to the Jew first and also to the Greek. Ethnic identity confers no spiritual standing before God.

section: I. Principles Extrapolated from Romans 9:6
text: 3. It is only after salvation through faith in Christ that the plan of God and the promises of God for Israel take effect. At the moment of salvation adjustment to the justice of God, the individual Jew receives the judicial imputation of divine righteousness and the judicial imputation of eternal life, and is therefore qualified for blessing from God. Prior to that moment, no covenant promise applies to him personally.

section: I. Principles Extrapolated from Romans 9:6
text: 4. Abraham became the first Jew at approximately age 99–100, at his circumcision. For the first ninety-nine years of his life Abraham was a Gentile — a Semitic Gentile of Sumero-Akkadian descent, descended from Noah through Shem. He had been a believer in Christ for many years before that point, and was already a mature believer when the Jewish race was formally inaugurated through him. The origin of the Jewish race therefore occurs in the X-radical but the definition of a true Jew requires Y- and Z-radicals.

section: I. Principles Extrapolated from Romans 9:6
text: 5. The fulfillment of the Abrahamic, Palestinian, Davidic, and New Covenants to Israel demands the imputation of divine righteousness and eternal life first. These covenants cannot be appropriated by racial Israel alone. They require regeneration. The promises are addressed to the spiritual seed of Abraham, not merely to the physical seed.

section: I. Principles Extrapolated from Romans 9:6
text: 6. The problem of Israel is compounded by the rejection of Christ as Savior. A racial Jew who rejects Christ remains permanently in the X-radical. He is not and cannot be a true Jew in the biblical sense, however impeccable his genealogy.

section: I. Principles Extrapolated from Romans 9:6
text: 7. Therefore, the real Jew is not the racial Jew but the born-again Jew — the Jew who believes in the Shekinah glory, the Lord Jesus Christ. In physical birth the Jew possesses the genetic line of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, but physical descent from Abraham does not constitute salvation. In regeneration the Jew receives the imputation of divine righteousness and eternal life, which anticipates a resurrection body and establishes the potential for blessing in time and eternity.

section: I. Principles Extrapolated from Romans 9:6
text: 8. The Y- and Z-radicals of the plan of God can only apply to the true Jew, that is, the Jew who has believed in the Lord Jesus Christ. The racial Jew lives in the X-radical. The true Jew lives in the Y- and Z-radicals. The equation X + Y + Z equals true Israel, but X alone yields only racial Israel.

section: II. The Plan of God: The X–Y–Z Equation
text: II. The Plan of God: The X–Y–Z Equation

section: II. The Plan of God: The X–Y–Z Equation
text: The interpretation of Romans 9 — and indeed of much of the New Testament epistle literature — is illuminated by a structural framework that can be expressed as a threefold equation. This framework tracks the progression of divine blessing from human birth through spiritual maturity to eternal reward.

section: X-Radical: Physical Birth and Condemnation
text: X-Radical: Physical Birth and Condemnation

section: X-Radical: Physical Birth and Condemnation
text: In the X-radical, all human beings begin at the same point. God imputes human life to the soul at physical birth. Simultaneously, Adam's original sin is imputed to the genetically formed old sin nature. These two imputations belong together: the old sin nature has its origin in Adam's original sin, and therefore there is perfect affinity between them — the imputed sin finds its proper home in the old sin nature.

section: X-Radical: Physical Birth and Condemnation
text: The imputation of Adam's original sin produces instant condemnation. This is not a punitive accident but an expression of the infinite wisdom and justice of God. Condemnation must precede justification. If God had imputed human life to the soul without simultaneously condemning the old sin nature through the imputation of Adam's sin, every human being who died before reaching moral accountability would have gone to eternal judgment with no recourse. Instead, by producing universal condemnation at birth, God simultaneously establishes universal eligibility for salvation. Every person who dies in infancy or before accountability is instantly saved, having been instantly condemned.

section: X-Radical: Physical Birth and Condemnation
text: Personal sins are never imputed to the individual for condemnation. God preserved every personal sin committed by every human being and imputed them all to Christ on the cross, where they were judged in him. The result is that no human being is ever condemned on the basis of his own personal sins — only on the basis of Adam's sin. This eliminates every ground of human merit, self-righteousness, or works-based salvation. God did the work in condemnation; God does the work in salvation.

section: Y-Radical: Salvation and Spiritual Growth
text: Y-Radical: Salvation and Spiritual Growth

section: Y-Radical: Salvation and Spiritual Growth
text: The Y-radical begins with salvation adjustment to the justice of God — the non-meritorious act of faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. At this moment two judicial imputations occur in sequence. First, all personal sins have already been imputed to Christ at the cross (judicial imputation 1). Second, divine righteousness is imputed to the believer at the moment of faith (judicial imputation 2). The imputation of divine righteousness establishes the potential for blessing from God: because the believer now possesses God's own righteousness, God can bless him without compromising any divine attribute.

section: Y-Radical: Salvation and Spiritual Growth
text: The Y-radical continues through the believer's advance in the plan of God by means of the consistent intake and application of Bible doctrine — the Grace Apparatus for Perception (GAP). The believer who persists in the perception of doctrine advances toward the maturity barrier and, upon cracking it, enters supergrace, the stage at which God imputes special blessing to his righteousness in six categories. Maturity adjustment to the justice of God through maximum doctrine resident in the soul is the second great adjustment of the plan of God.

section: Z-Radical: Eternity and Resurrection
text: Z-Radical: Eternity and Resurrection

section: Z-Radical: Eternity and Resurrection
text: The Z-radical encompasses eternity: the resurrection body, the judgment seat of Christ, and the imputation of eternal blessing and reward. For the true Jew — the regenerate Jew — the Z-radical includes the fulfillment of all four unconditional covenants: the Abrahamic covenant (blessing to the world through Abraham's seed), the Palestinian covenant (a specific land grant in perpetuity), the Davidic covenant (the rule of Messiah, the Son of David, over Israel), and the New Covenant to Israel (the internalization of the law and the full experience of divine blessing in the kingdom). None of these covenants can be appropriated by racial Israel in the X-radical. They require the eternal life and imputed righteousness that are received only through faith in Christ.

section: III. The Concept of the True Jew
text: III. The Concept of the True Jew

section: III. The Concept of the True Jew
text: Two concepts must be clearly established before the argument of Romans 9:7–18 can be understood: the origin of Israel and the biblical definition of the true Jew.

section: Definition of the True Jew
text: Definition of the True Jew

section: Definition of the True Jew
text: 1. True Israel is composed of the children of God rather than the children of Abraham. Galatians 3:26 states: 'You are all children of God through faith in Christ Jesus.' The divine election of Israel is therefore limited to those racial Jews who have been born again through faith in Christ.

section: Definition of the True Jew
text: 2. Racial Jews live in the X-radical; true Jews live in the Y- and Z-radicals. Physical birth with the genes of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob qualifies a person to be a racial Jew — a member of the Jewish ethnic and national entity. It does not make him a true Jew. The true Jew is defined by regeneration.

section: Definition of the True Jew
text: 3. The true Jew, through physical birth, possesses the genes of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; and through regeneration, possesses the God of Abraham — the Lord Jesus Christ, the Shekinah glory. This is the complete and authoritative definition.

section: Definition of the True Jew
text: 4. Election cannot be disassociated from eternal salvation. The omniscience of God in eternity past knew every actual choice that every individual would ever make. Only the actual was entered into the divine decree. Thus the election of Israel runs through the line of regeneration, not through the line of physical descent. Jacob was elected because he believed; Esau was not elected because he did not believe. The distinction is not arbitrary — it reflects the actual exercise of human volition as known by the omniscience of God.

section: Definition of the True Jew
text: 5. Salvation adjustment to the justice of God through faith in Jesus Christ is the qualification for the election of Israel. What is said of election is equally true of foreknowledge and foreordination. The promises of the Word of God are valid only to regenerate Israel, not to racial Israel.

section: Definition of the True Jew
text: 6. Regeneration, not primogeniture, is the issue. Primogeniture — the exclusive right of inheritance belonging to the firstborn — is a human legal principle that operates in the X-radical. It has no force in the Y- and Z-radicals. Ishmael was the firstborn son of Abraham but could not inherit because he was not born again. Isaac was the second son but became the heir because he believed in the Lord Jesus Christ. Similarly, Esau was the firstborn twin but remained in the X-radical; Jacob, the second, believed and was born again, and God in anticipation of his maturity changed his name to Israel. The distinction between the twins is the same as the distinction between the sons of Abraham: one twin remained a Gentile in the X-radical; the other became a true Jew in the Y-radical.

section: IV. Romans 9:7 — Grammatical and Lexical Analysis
text: IV. Romans 9:7 — Grammatical and Lexical Analysis

section: IV. Romans 9:7 — Grammatical and Lexical Analysis
text: Verse 7 introduces the first of three case histories that will occupy Paul through verse 18: the sons of Abraham. The verse begins with a negative conjunction and a causal clause, and sets up the controlling principle that physical descent from Abraham is not the criterion for inheritance.

section: The Negative Conjunction
text: The Negative Conjunction

section: The Negative Conjunction
text: The verse opens with the negative conjunction oude (οὐδέ), compounded from ou and de, meaning 'not even' or 'neither.' This is a strong negation that reinforces the denial of the preceding verse: not only has the word of God not failed, but not even descent from Abraham constitutes the criterion for true Jewish identity.

section: The Causal Conjunction hoti
text: The Causal Conjunction hoti

section: The Causal Conjunction hoti
text: Following the negative is the causal conjunction hoti (ὅτι), here functioning to introduce a causal clause: 'neither because' or 'not even because.' The full phrase rendered together: 'neither because they are Abraham's seed.'

section: The Verb eimi
text: The Verb eimi

section: The Verb eimi
text: The verb is the present active indicative of eimi (εἰμί), the verb of being. The present tense is durative — it denotes a state that began in the past and continues into the present. The state in view is the existence of the Jewish race, which began with Abraham's circumcision and has continued through Isaac, Jacob, the twelve patriarchs, and all subsequent generations. The active voice assigns the action to the racial Jew who possesses the genes of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. The indicative mood is declarative, asserting the historical reality of the Jewish race.

section: The Noun sperma
text: The Noun sperma

section: The Noun sperma
text: The predicate nominative is the singular noun sperma (σπέρμα), meaning 'seed,' 'posterity,' or 'descendants.' In this context it refers to the physical seed of Abraham — the racial Jew descended from Abraham through Isaac and Jacob and the twelve patriarchs. The undeclinable proper noun Abraam (Ἀβραάμ) follows immediately.

section: The Adjective pas and the Noun teknon
text: The Adjective pas and the Noun teknon

section: The Adjective pas and the Noun teknon
text: 'All' renders the nominative plural of pas (πᾶς), referring comprehensively to all racial Jews — all who possess the genetic line of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and the twelve patriarchs. The predicate nominative plural tekna (τέκνα), the plural of teknon (τέκνον), means 'children' in the sense of 'children of inheritance.' In this verse teknon is used for believers in Christ — those who are children in the sense of possessing the inheritance. The verse therefore asserts that not all racial Jews are children of the inheritance.

section: Corrected Translation of Romans 9:7a
text: Corrected Translation of Romans 9:7a

section: Corrected Translation of Romans 9:7a
text: Neither because they are Abraham's seed — that is, his posterity, his descendants — are they all children of the inheritance.

section: V. The Sons of Abraham: Eight Sons, Three Mothers
text: V. The Sons of Abraham: Eight Sons, Three Mothers

section: V. The Sons of Abraham: Eight Sons, Three Mothers
text: The claim that physical descent from Abraham is not sufficient for inheritance is immediately illustrated by the fact that Abraham had eight sons by three different women. The natural question is: why did one son inherit rather than the others? The answer that suggests itself to human viewpoint — legitimacy of birth, quality of the mother, degree of affection — is exactly wrong in every case.

section: V. The Sons of Abraham: Eight Sons, Three Mothers
text: Abraham's eight sons are as follows. By Hagar, the Egyptian slave woman: Ishmael (Genesis 16). By Sarah, the Sumero-Akkadian princess who became the first Jewish woman at the same moment Abraham became the first Jew: Isaac (Genesis 21). By Keturah, the Arabian woman with whom Abraham lived after Sarah's death: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shua (Genesis 25:1–2).

section: V. The Sons of Abraham: Eight Sons, Three Mothers
text: Ishmael was the firstborn. The six sons of Keturah appear to have been born outside of formal marriage. Isaac was the son of the legitimate wife and covenant partner. By every principle of human law and social expectation, Ishmael had the strongest claim, Isaac the clearest legal claim, and the sons of Keturah the weakest claim of all.

section: V. The Sons of Abraham: Eight Sons, Three Mothers
text: None of that determined the inheritance. Genesis 25:5 states plainly: 'Abraham gave all that he had to Isaac.' Not because Isaac was the legitimate son. Not because Sarah was a better woman than Hagar or Keturah — the text nowhere makes this claim or implies it. Not because of any virtue on the part of any of the mothers. Motherhood is confined to the X-radical. It cannot move a person into the Y- or Z-radicals. The virtue or character of a mother has no bearing on the eternal standing of her children. Each individual must make his or her own adjustment to the justice of God.

section: V. The Sons of Abraham: Eight Sons, Three Mothers
text: Isaac inherited because he was born again. He believed in the Lord Jesus Christ — Jehovah Elohim, the God of Abraham — and thereby became a true Jew and a child of the inheritance. Ishmael rejected Christ and remained a Semitic Gentile in the X-radical. The sons of Keturah similarly did not believe and remained in the X-radical. The criterion is regeneration, not genealogy, not legitimacy, not maternal quality, and not birth order.

section: V. The Sons of Abraham: Eight Sons, Three Mothers
text: This same principle is then applied with even greater precision to the case of the twins Esau and Jacob, which will be developed beginning in verse 10. Both twins were born to the same mother, Rebekah, making the genealogical argument even more clearly inapplicable. The distinction between them cannot be traced to maternal virtue, birth order, or legal status — it can only be traced to the actual choices they made with respect to the God of Israel.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Nine
text: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Nine

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Nine
text: 1. The word of God has not failed with respect to Israel because the promises were never addressed to racial Israel as such but to regenerate Israel — the true Jew who has believed in the Lord Jesus Christ.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Nine
text: 2. Two Israels must be consistently distinguished: racial Israel (the physical descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, living in the X-radical) and true Israel (regenerate Jews living in the Y- and Z-radicals, qualified for all four unconditional covenants).

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Nine
text: 3. The true Jew is defined by two things simultaneously: through physical birth, possession of the genes of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; and through regeneration, possession of the God of Abraham — the Lord Jesus Christ, the Shekinah glory.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Nine
text: 4. Salvation adjustment to the justice of God through faith in Christ is the sole qualification for entry into the Y-radical and for participation in the election and promises of Israel. This is the consistent teaching of the Old Testament as well as the New: Abraham believed God and it was credited to him as righteousness (Genesis 15:6).

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Nine
text: 5. The divine election of Israel runs through the line of regeneration, not primogeniture. Ishmael was the firstborn of Abraham but did not inherit. Isaac was the second son but inherited. Esau was the firstborn twin but did not inherit. Jacob was the second twin but inherited. In each case the determining factor was faith in Christ, not birth order or legal status.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Nine
text: 6. The imputation of Adam's original sin at physical birth is an act of divine wisdom and grace, not injustice. Universal condemnation at birth establishes universal eligibility for salvation and ensures that every person who dies before moral accountability is saved instantly, having been instantly condemned. It also eliminates every ground of human merit in either condemnation or salvation.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Nine
text: 7. Personal sins are never the basis of individual condemnation before God. All personal sins were imputed to Christ at the cross and judged there. The only sin that condemns is Adam's original sin, imputed at birth. This is the structural reason why salvation is purely by grace through faith and cannot involve human works.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Nine
text: 8. The grammatical analysis of Romans 9:7a confirms the doctrinal content: the durative present tense of eimi establishes the ongoing existence of racial Israel as a historical reality; sperma identifies the physical seed of Abraham; and teknon in the sense of 'children of inheritance' identifies only the regenerate — those who have believed in Christ.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Nine
text: 9. Motherhood, birth legitimacy, and maternal character have no bearing on eternal standing. Each individual stands before God on the basis of his or her own volition with respect to the gospel. No human relationship — filial, maternal, or ancestral — can convey salvation or convey the promises of God.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Sixty-Nine
text: 10. The anti-Semitic use of Romans 9 to argue that God is finished with racial Israel is a fundamental misreading of the passage. Paul's point is precisely the opposite: God's faithfulness to Israel is vindicated because His promises were always addressed to the true Israel — the regenerate — and that remnant has always existed and will always exist, extending through the millennial kingdom and into eternity.

section: Romans 9:7 — The True Jew: Election, Regeneration, and the Seed of Abraham
text: Romans 9 stands at the center of Paul's most sustained and demanding argument in the entire epistle. Three chapters form a single unit: chapter 9 treats Israel as elect in part; chapter 10, Israel as presently rejected; chapter 11, Israel as accepted in the future. Within chapter 9, the second paragraph — the premise that 'all Israel is not Israel' (verse 6) — is now being illustrated by the formation of the Jewish nation itself. The exegesis of verse 7 opens that illustration.

section: I. The Outline of Romans 9
text: I. The Outline of Romans 9

section: I. The Outline of Romans 9
text: Five paragraphs organize the chapter. The first, verses 1–5, establishes the uniqueness of Israel and Paul's great burden for his own people. The second, verse 6, states the governing premise: not all who are descended from Israel are truly Israel. The third, verses 7–18, illustrates that premise from the formation of the Jewish race and nation. The fourth, verses 19–29, illustrates the same premise from the essence of God. The fifth, verses 30–33, illustrates the premise from the salvation of the Gentiles.

section: I. The Outline of Romans 9
text: The corrected translation of verses 1–6 provides the foundation. Paul affirms that he communicates doctrine without lying, his conscience bearing joint testimony with him in the Holy Spirit, that he has a great sorrow and a constant pain in his right lobe. He could wish — though it cannot be — that he himself were accursed and separated from Christ for the sake of his racial brethren, the Jews, his fellow countrymen according to earthly descent. They are Israelites, to whom belong the adoption, the Shekinah glory, the unconditional covenants, the gift of the Mosaic law as establishment, the true worship of God, and the promises that emphasize the integrity of God. From them are the regenerate ancestors — Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob — and from them, according to the flesh, is the Christ, the one who came in the flesh, who is God, ruler over all, extolled and praised forever. Yet this is not to imply that the word of God has failed; for not all who are descended from Israel are truly Israel.

section: II. Review of the Doctrine of the True Jew
text: II. Review of the Doctrine of the True Jew

section: II. Review of the Doctrine of the True Jew
text: Before moving into the exegesis of verse 7, it is necessary to review the doctrine of the true Jew, since all that follows in Romans 9 depends upon the distinction between the racial Jew and the true Jew.

section: Point 1 — Composition of the True Jew
text: Point 1 — Composition of the True Jew

section: Point 1 — Composition of the True Jew
text: The true Jew is composed of the children of God rather than merely the children of Abraham. The divine election of Israel is therefore limited to those racial Jews who have been born again through faith in Christ. The line of Israel is unique in its very origin. Abraham was the first Jew. He was approximately one hundred years old when God constituted him a Jew — prior to that he was a Gentile, a Sumerian, a Chaldean. He became a Jew after he had cracked the maturity barrier, as an expression of divine blessing imputed to him by the justice of God. The race of Israel is therefore absolutely unique in its origin.

section: Point 1 — Composition of the True Jew
text: Abraham had eight sons by three different women. Only one of those eight is the source of the Jewish race; the remaining seven are Gentiles. To press the point further: in the third generation there is a single mother, Rebekah, bearing twins. Jacob is in the line of Israel — his name was changed to

section: Point 1 — Composition of the True Jew
text: Yisra'el, a prince of God — while his twin brother Esau, though the firstborn by primogeniture, was set aside and remained a Gentile. The secret was not in physical birth or maternal lineage but in regeneration.

section: Point 2 — The X, Y, Z Radical Framework and the True Jew
text: Point 2 — The X, Y, Z Radical Framework and the True Jew

section: Point 2 — The X, Y, Z Radical Framework and the True Jew
text: All racial Jews exist in X-radical. X-radical is defined as: the imputation of human life to the soul at birth + the imputation of Adam's original sin + pertinent gospel doctrine = the first hope, the absolute confidence that faith in Christ produces eternal life. Salvation adjustment to the justice of God through faith in the Shekinah glory, the Lord Jesus Christ, terminates the first hope and makes it a reality.

section: Point 2 — The X, Y, Z Radical Framework and the True Jew
text: The true Jew moves into Y-radical: Judicial Imputation One — the imputation of all personal sins to Christ on the cross — plus Judicial Imputation Two — the imputation of God's perfect righteousness to every person who believes in Christ. The possession of divine righteousness creates the second potential: divine blessing in time, imputed by the justice of God to the righteousness of God resident in the believer. With maximum doctrine resident in the soul — the maturity adjustment — this second potential is realized.

section: Point 2 — The X, Y, Z Radical Framework and the True Jew
text: Z-radical follows: the imputation of eternal life + the imputation of blessing in time at maturity and thereafter + undeserved suffering that focuses the believer on eternity = the third hope, the absolute confidence that at resurrection the mature believer will receive the imputation of eternal blessing and reward. This is the seventh imputation. This is the true Jew.

section: Point 2 — The X, Y, Z Radical Framework and the True Jew
text: The racial Jew is found in X-radical. The true Jew has advanced into Y and Z-radicals in the plan of God. This is the place of true Israel —

section: Point 3 — Election Cannot Be Disassociated from Eternal Salvation
text: Point 3 — Election Cannot Be Disassociated from Eternal Salvation

section: Point 3 — Election Cannot Be Disassociated from Eternal Salvation
text: Billions of years before creation, the omniscience of God had perfect and total cognizance of not only what would happen — actuality — but also of every alternative — probability. Only actuality was fed into the computer of the divine decrees. The omniscience of God knew every Jew who would believe in Christ; the printout reads election, foreknowledge, and predestination. He also knew every Jew who would possess the genes of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, but would remain in X-radical, rejecting the Shekinah glory; the printout for these is condemnation. Election therefore cannot be disassociated from eternal salvation.

section: Point 4 — Salvation Adjustment as the Qualification for Election
text: Point 4 — Salvation Adjustment as the Qualification for Election

section: Point 4 — Salvation Adjustment as the Qualification for Election
text: Salvation adjustment to the justice of God through faith in the Lord Jesus Christ is the qualification for the election of Israel. God will keep His word and fulfill His promises — both in time during the millennium and in eternity thereafter — to all Jews who are in the election, who are therefore foreknown as elect and foreordained through the omniscience of God. The promises of the word of God are valid only to regenerate Israel, not to the racial Jew who has not believed.

section: Point 5 — Isaac Distinguished from Ishmael through Regeneration
text: Point 5 — Isaac Distinguished from Ishmael through Regeneration

section: Point 5 — Isaac Distinguished from Ishmael through Regeneration
text: Isaac is distinguished from Ishmael, and Jacob is distinguished from Esau, through regeneration, not through birth order or maternal lineage. Esau is a vessel of wrath. Jacob is a vessel of mercy. The distinction between the two will be developed in the difficult anacolutha of verses 22–24, which represents the most challenging grammatical and exegetical passage in the entire Greek New Testament.

section: Point 6 — Regeneration, Not Primogeniture, Is the Issue
text: Point 6 — Regeneration, Not Primogeniture, Is the Issue

section: Point 6 — Regeneration, Not Primogeniture, Is the Issue
text: Primogeniture is the exclusive right of inheritance belonging to the firstborn. The true Jew, through physical birth, possesses the genes of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; through regeneration he possesses the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob — the Shekinah glory, whom the Jews call

section: Point 6 — Regeneration, Not Primogeniture, Is the Issue
text: Adonai Elohim, the Lord Jesus Christ, the God of Israel. Regeneration, not primogeniture, is the issue.

section: III. Exegesis of Romans 9:7 — 'Neither Because They Are Abraham's Seed'
text: III. Exegesis of Romans 9:7 — 'Neither Because They Are Abraham's Seed'

section: The Negative Conjunction
text: The Negative Conjunction

section: The Negative Conjunction
text: The verse opens with the negative conjunction οὐδέ (oude), which functions here as neither, introducing a subordinate clause of negation. The conjunction ὅτι (hoti) follows as a causal conjunction translatable because. Taken together: neither because.

section: The Predicate Noun: Sperma
text: The Predicate Noun: Sperma

section: The Predicate Noun: Sperma
text: The predicate nominative is the dative singular of σπέρμα (sperma), meaning seed or posterity. Here it refers specifically to the physical seed of Abraham — racial Jews, those who possess the genes of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, descended from one of the twelve patriarchs from whom came the thirteen tribes. Being a racial Jew is defined entirely by physical descent, not by spiritual condition.

section: The Nominative Plural: Tekna
text: The Nominative Plural: Tekna

section: The Nominative Plural: Tekna
text: The nominative plural τέκνα (tekna), from τέκνον (teknon), means children in the sense of children of inheritance. Jews who have not been born again do not inherit. Inheritance is not on the basis of physical birth but on the basis of regeneration. Abraham had eight sons; only Isaac was the child of inheritance. Genesis 25:5 states: Now Abraham gave all that he had to Isaac.

section: The Nominative Plural: Tekna
text: Corrected translation of this portion: Neither because they are Abraham's seed are all racial Jews children of the inheritance.

section: IV. The Adversative: 'But in Isaac Shall Your Seed Be Called'
text: IV. The Adversative: 'But in Isaac Shall Your Seed Be Called'

section: The Adversative Conjunction
text: The Adversative Conjunction

section: The Adversative Conjunction
text: The second half of the verse is introduced by the adversative conjunction ἀλλά (alla), but, which sets up a sharp contrast between Isaac and all the other children of Abraham. Isaac is unique among the eight sons; therefore the race of Israel that proceeds through him is unique. This clause quotes Genesis 21:12, which is also cited in Hebrews 11:18.

section: The Name Yitzhak
text: The Name Yitzhak

section: The Name Yitzhak
text: The preposition ἐν (en) is followed by the indeclinable proper noun Ἰσαάκ (Isaak), a transliteration of the Hebrew Yitzhak, meaning laughter. The name derives from the account in Genesis 18, where Sarah, listening to the conversation between Abraham and the angel of the Lord, laughed inwardly upon hearing that she, past the age of childbearing, would conceive. The Lord heard her inward laughter and announced the child would be called laughter. When the child was born, Sarah's laughter was fulfilled: she had laughter in her womb, and then laughter throughout the household.

section: The Noun Sperma and the Verb Kaleitai
text: The Noun Sperma and the Verb Kaleitai

section: The Noun Sperma and the Verb Kaleitai
text: Following the proper noun comes the nominative singular subject σπέρμα (sperma) again, with the dative singular indirect object from the personal pronoun σοί (soi), to you. Literally: a seed to you in Isaac, an idiom for your seed in Isaac. The verb is the future passive indicative of καλέω (kaleō), which means to call, to designate, to name. In the passive, it carries the connotation of election: to be called, to be designated, to be elected. This is a gnomic future tense — a statement of absolute doctrinal fact. The passive voice indicates that Abraham's racial descendants receive the action: they are designated or elected through Isaac. The indicative mood declares historical reality.

section: The Noun Sperma and the Verb Kaleitai
text: Corrected translation of the full verse: Neither because they are Abraham's seed are all racial Jews children of the inheritance; but in Isaac your seed shall be elected or designated.

section: V. Principles Arising from Romans 9:7
text: V. Principles Arising from Romans 9:7

section: The Origin of the Jewish Race
text: The Origin of the Jewish Race

section: The Origin of the Jewish Race
text: Principle 1: The Jewish race began with Abraham's attainment of spiritual maturity, represented by his circumcision at approximately one hundred years of age. Every other race among the nations traces its origin to physical birth — descent from Noah through Shem, Ham, or Japheth. Abraham's origin as a Jew is different: he was in Z-radical when God took the Gentile Abraham, a Sumerian-Chaldean, and constituted him a Jew. The origin of the Jewish race is therefore spiritual, not physical, and is superior to the origin of any other race. That very superiority carries a proportionally greater responsibility: those who possess the genes of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob bear the responsibility of believing in the Lord Jesus Christ, for the promises of God are to the spiritual seed of Abraham — those who possess eternal life and divine righteousness — not to the physical seed alone.

section: The Origin of the Jewish Race
text: Principle 2: The Jewish race originated with those who believed in Jehovah Elohim, the Shekinah glory, the Lord Jesus Christ. Abraham is the first Jew; his brother Nahor remained a Gentile and a Chaldean. Abraham, as a believer, prints out under the categories of election, foreknowledge, and predestination in the divine decrees.

section: The Origin of the Jewish Race
text: Principle 3: Isaac was the natural and spiritual seed of Abraham. Both Isaac and Ishmael had self-determination through the function of their own free will. Ishmael, the firstborn under primogeniture, should under natural law have been the heir. But Ishmael remained in X-radical. He did not possess either the imputed righteousness of God or eternal life. Isaac moved from X-radical into Y-radical and ultimately Z-radical, becoming the true Jew and the vehicle for the perpetuation of the race in the next generation.

section: The Origin of the Jewish Race
text: Principle 4: To be an heir of the promises of God, one must possess both the righteousness of God and the life of God — eternal life. God's perfect righteousness is the target for the justice of God's imputed blessing. Justice demands righteousness as the home of its benefactions. God as Elohim was free to impute blessing to Abraham because Abraham had the righteousness of God from the moment of faith — Genesis 15:6 records this, though the imputation had occurred even earlier, before Genesis 12, while Abraham was still a Gentile. To be an heir of the promises, one must possess divine righteousness for temporal blessing and eternal life for the everlasting fulfillment of the Abrahamic covenant.

section: The Origin of the Jewish Race
text: Principle 5: The righteousness of God and eternal life are imputed only at salvation adjustment to the justice of God through faith in Christ. There is no other mechanism and no other moment.

section: Omniscience, Decrees, and Free Will
text: Omniscience, Decrees, and Free Will

section: Omniscience, Decrees, and Free Will
text: Principle 6: Since the omniscience of God knew that Isaac would believe in the Shekinah glory — Adonai Elohim, the God of Israel — and that Ishmael would reject Christ, He entered the facts of history into the computer of the divine decrees before time began. It could theoretically have gone the other way. The alternative existed: if Isaac had said no and Ishmael had said yes, the line of Israel would have run through Ishmael. But that is unreality — probability, not actuality. Probability is never entered into the divine decrees, though God knows every alternative down to the last generation of history.

section: Omniscience, Decrees, and Free Will
text: Principle 7: Election, foreknowledge, and predestination are theological categories that merely acknowledge what is in the computer of the divine decrees. Foreknowledge is not omniscience. The foreknowledge of God makes nothing certain; it merely acknowledges what is already certain by virtue of what is in the decrees. Omniscience knows the knowable — actual and possible — simultaneously and comprehensively. Foreknowledge acknowledges only what is actual. Neither election nor predestination makes anything certain in themselves; they are printouts of what omniscience has already perceived and the decrees already contain.

section: Omniscience, Decrees, and Free Will
text: Principle 8: The omniscience of God knows the free will of every person and every decision that will occur at any moment of history. He knows the result of every decision and also knows what would have been the result had free will chosen any alternative. Nothing is unknown to God. Only what actually occurs is entered into the decrees.

section: Omniscience, Decrees, and Free Will
text: Principle 9: Only Isaac's decision to believe in Christ was entered into the computer of the divine decrees, resulting in Isaac being elected as the vehicle for the perpetuation of the Jewish race. Genesis 17:21: But my covenant I will establish with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear to you at this season next year. Genesis 21:12: For in Isaac your seed will be called. Hebrews 11:18: In Isaac your seed shall be called.

section: Omniscience, Decrees, and Free Will
text: Principle 10: This is why the God of the Jews is designated the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. The sacred divine name — the Tetragrammaton, which Israel does not pronounce, substituting

section: Omniscience, Decrees, and Free Will
text: Adonai in its place — carries the vowel points of the verb to be, yielding the rendering I AM THAT I AM. The Lord Jesus Christ is the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the Shekinah glory who dwelt between the cherubim in the Holy of Holies, who came in the flesh (John 1:14), and who is the object of faith for every true Jew.

section: The Election of Israel Among the Four Dispensational Elections
text: The Election of Israel Among the Four Dispensational Elections

section: The Election of Israel Among the Four Dispensational Elections
text: Principle 11: The foundation of the Jewish race is unique and forms one of the two elections specified by dispensation as particularly prominent in Scripture — the election of Israel and the election of the church, the royal family of God. There are in fact four elections altogether: the election of Gentile believers, the election of Israel in the dispensation of Israel, the election of the church in the church age, and the election of millennial saints. But the election of Israel, originating with regeneration as its foundation, is the subject here.

section: The Election of Israel Among the Four Dispensational Elections
text: Principle 12: Since Israel is an election of God, it must originate with regeneration — the possession of eternal life and the potentiality of divine blessing. The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the Lord Jesus Christ, is the secret to being true Israel. All Israel is not Israel. Only those Jews who have the genes of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and who have believed in the Lord Jesus Christ are under the election and therefore beneficiaries of the promises of God.

section: The Election of Israel Among the Four Dispensational Elections
text: Principle 13: The word of God has not failed the Jews. Rather, the Jews who depend upon the Mosaic law and the functions of Judaism for salvation have failed the word of God by rejecting the Lord Jesus Christ, who is the Shekinah glory, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. This is the great burden of the Apostle Paul expressed in verses 1–5 — the burden of any believer who understands that those he loves are so close by virtue of heritage and yet so far by virtue of unbelief.

section: VI. Israel, the Nations, and Anti-Semitism
text: VI. Israel, the Nations, and Anti-Semitism

section: VI. Israel, the Nations, and Anti-Semitism
text: The promises of the Abrahamic, Palestinian, Davidic, and New covenants will all be fulfilled at the second advent of Christ. The Shekinah glory that dwelt between the cherubim in the Holy of Holies — the mercy seat whose covering blood satisfied the justice of God on the Day of Atonement — came in the flesh (John 1:14). For three years, the nation of Israel had the Shekinah glory face to face: His miracles, His teaching, His person. Many rejected Him. The weight of negative volition was sufficient to trigger the fifth cycle of discipline, executed in 70 AD after forty years of warning — including the sign gift of tongues, which gave the gospel to diaspora Jews in Gentile languages and ceased on the day Jerusalem fell.

section: VI. Israel, the Nations, and Anti-Semitism
text: From 70 AD until the second advent, only Gentile nations can function as client nations to God — this is the Times of the Gentiles. During this period, one of the responsibilities of every Gentile client nation is to provide a haven for Israel: the same freedom, the same legal protections, and the same opportunities afforded to its own citizens. The reason is theological: Satan's primary strategic objective includes the destruction of the Jewish people, because the existence of the Jewish people is the precondition for the fulfillment of the unconditional covenants at the second advent. Anti-Semitism in any form — whether ideological, political, or social — is satanic in origin and satanic in purpose. There is no such thing as a Jewish conspiracy; there is no racial solution to any social or political problem. The causes of the world's difficulties are two: Satan as the ruler of this world, and the old sin nature resident in every human being. Any other accounting is propaganda. Believers are to respond to Israel with thoughtfulness, compassion, and the consistent defense of Israel's legal freedom and security within any nation they inhabit.

section: VI. Israel, the Nations, and Anti-Semitism
text: At the second advent, the nation of Israel will again become the client nation of God. The 144,000 Jewish evangelists of the Tribulation carry out a special mission of world evangelism precisely because no Jewish client nation can exist during the Times of the Gentiles. The second advent terminates the dispensation of Israel's interruption and resumes its conclusion — a millennium of one thousand years under the direct reign of the Lord Jesus Christ, followed by eternity.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy
text: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy
text: 1. The racial Jew and the true Jew are distinct categories. The racial Jew is defined by physical descent from Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob — the possession of their genes through the four generations of the patriarchs. The true Jew is defined by regeneration — faith in Adonai Elohim, the Lord Jesus Christ, the Shekinah glory, the God of Israel. Every racial Jew begins in X-radical. The true Jew moves into Y and Z-radicals through salvation adjustment to the justice of God.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy
text: 2. The origin of the Jewish race is spiritual, not physical. Abraham was constituted a Jew not by birth but by his cracking of the maturity barrier and the subsequent divine imputation of blessing. Every other race traces its origin to physical birth. The Jewish race traces its origin to spiritual reality — faith and regeneration. This uniqueness entails a commensurate responsibility: the physical seed of Abraham must possess the God of Abraham through faith in order to inherit the promises.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy
text: 3. The distinction between Isaac and Ishmael turns entirely on regeneration. Primogeniture, maternal lineage, and birth order are all irrelevant. Ishmael was the firstborn; he was not the heir. Isaac was the second-born; he was the heir. The difference: Isaac believed in Adonai Elohim and thereby received the imputation of divine righteousness and eternal life. Ishmael did not. Ishmael and the children of Keturah are the source of many Arab nations; they are Gentiles, not Jews, though their origin is Semitic.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy
text: 4. To be an heir of the promises of God, one must possess divine righteousness and eternal life. The justice of God imputes blessing only to the righteousness of God. God's justice cannot impute blessing to a sinful nature or to human merit. Only the imputation of divine righteousness at salvation — the moment of faith in Christ — creates the proper target for divine blessing in time. And only the imputation of eternal life at that same moment qualifies the true Jew for the eternal fulfillment of the Abrahamic covenant.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy
text: 5. The divine decrees contain only actuality, never mere probability. The omniscience of God knows every alternative decision that any human being could ever make, including what would have happened if Isaac had rejected Christ and Ishmael had believed. But only what actually occurs is entered into the computer of the divine decrees. Election, foreknowledge, and predestination are theological categories that acknowledge the content of the decrees; they do not make anything certain in themselves. Omniscience perceives; the decrees record what omniscience has perceived as actual.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy
text: 6. The verb kaleō in the future passive indicative carries the force of divine election. The phrase 'in Isaac your seed shall be called' is not merely a naming formula but a declaration of election. The passive voice indicates that the descendants of Abraham receive the action — they are designated, elected, set apart — through Isaac. The gnomic future tense states this as an absolute doctrinal fact. Genesis 21:12 and Hebrews 11:18 confirm the same point.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy
text: 7. The word of God has not failed; the racial Jew who rejects Christ has failed the word of God. Paul's burden in Romans 9:1–5 is precisely this: those who have the heritage of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob — the adoption, the Shekinah glory, the unconditional covenants, the law, the worship, the promises, the patriarchs, and the very humanity of Christ — are so close and yet so far. The promises of God are valid only for regenerate Israel. The racial Jew who depends upon law-keeping or the functions of Judaism for standing before God has rejected the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob — the Lord Jesus Christ.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy
text: 8. Anti-Semitism in any form is satanic propaganda. Satan's strategic interest in the destruction of the Jewish people is directly related to the unconditional covenants whose fulfillment at the second advent requires a living Jewish remnant. One of the obligations of a Gentile client nation is to provide a haven of freedom and legal protection for Israel. Believers are to maintain toward Israel an attitude of thoughtfulness, compassion, and legal advocacy, and to reject any form of racial conspiracy theory as inconsistent with the word of God and complicit with satanic objectives.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy
text: 9. The Shekinah glory is the Lord Jesus Christ, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. The cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night over the tabernacle, the presence between the cherubim above the mercy seat and the ark of the covenant, the one who is never pronounced by the Tetragrammaton but addressed as Adonai — this is the Lord Jesus Christ. When He came in the flesh (John 1:14), He was the Shekinah glory incarnate. The Jews who had said for generations that everything would be different if they could see Him face to face saw Him for three years and the majority still rejected Him. This is the tragedy that Paul carries as a constant pain in his right lobe.
