section: Romans 9:1–9 | The Divine Decrees, Foreknowledge, and the Will of God
text: Romans 9:1–9 | The Divine Decrees, Foreknowledge, and the Will of God

section: Romans 9:1–9 | The Divine Decrees, Foreknowledge, and the Will of God
text: Romans 9:1–9 “I am speaking the truth in Christ—I am not lying; my conscience bears me witness in the Holy Spirit—that I have great sorrow and unceasing anguish in my heart. For I could wish that I myself were accursed and cut off from Christ for the sake of my brothers, my kinsmen according to the flesh. They are Israelites, and to them belong the adoption, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law, the worship, and the promises. To them belong the patriarchs, and from their race, according to the flesh, is the Christ, who is God over all, blessed forever. Amen. But it is not as though the word of God has failed. For not all who are descended from Israel belong to Israel, and not all are children of Abraham because they are his offspring, but 'Through Isaac shall your offspring be named.' This means that it is not the children of the flesh who are the children of God, but the children of the promise are counted as offspring. For this is what the promise said: 'About this time next year I will return, and Sarah shall have a son.' And not only so, but also when Rebekah had conceived children by one man, our forefather Isaac...” (ESV)

section: Romans 9:1–9 | The Divine Decrees, Foreknowledge, and the Will of God
text: Corrected translation: I am communicating doctrine, I am not lying; my conscience bearing joint testimony with me in the Holy Spirit, that I have a great sorrow and constant pain in my right lobe, for I could wish that I myself would be a curse — consequently separated from Christ — it cannot be — for the sake of my brethren, racial Jews, my fellow countrymen, national Jews, according to earthly descent, who are Israelites, to whom is the adoption and the Shekinah glory and the covenants and the gift of the law and the worship of the true God and the promises, from whom are the regenerative ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, in fact from whom is the Christ, the one who came in the flesh, the one who was God, ruler over all, extolled, praised, eulogized forever, amen. However, this is not to imply that the word of God has failed, for not all who are descended from Israel are really Israel, neither because they are Abraham's seed are all racial Jews children of the inheritance. But — 'In Isaac your seed shall be designated' — this means that the descendants of the flesh are not the children of God but the children of the promise are imputed for the seed. For the word of promise is this: 'At this time — maturity adjustment to the justice of God — I will come to impute blessing, and Sarah will have a son.'

section: Romans 9:1–9 | The Divine Decrees, Foreknowledge, and the Will of God
text: Romans 9 resumes Paul's demonstration that the word of God has not failed with respect to Israel. The chapter opens with Paul's personal anguish over his kinsmen according to the flesh and catalogues the covenantal privileges belonging to Israel. The exegesis of verses 1–9 raises immediate questions about the relationship between divine sovereignty and human free will, between the eternal decrees of God and the historical experience of the nation. Before advancing to verse 10, this chapter develops the foundational theological framework — the doctrine of the divine decrees, the foreknowledge of God, and the will of God — without which the argumentation of Romans 9–11 cannot be rightly understood.

section: I. The Shekinah Glory and Its Significance for Israel
text: I. The Shekinah Glory and Its Significance for Israel

section: I. The Shekinah Glory and Its Significance for Israel
text: Among the privileges catalogued in verses 3–5, the Shekinah glory occupies a unique position. The Shekinah was the visible manifestation of the Lord Jesus Christ as the God of Israel. During the wilderness period it appeared as a cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night, positioned above the Holy of Holies in the tabernacle. The two cherubim flanking the mercy seat each represented one of the two divine attributes constituting divine holiness — righteousness and justice — and it was between these cherubim that the Shekinah glory dwelt.

section: I. The Shekinah Glory and Its Significance for Israel
text: Access to the Shekinah was restricted to the high priest, once per year, on the Day of Atonement. The high priest would sprinkle blood over the mercy seat, a typological representation of propitiation. Apart from that single annual entrance, the Shekinah remained hidden behind the veil. No Israelite saw the Shekinah glory directly until the incarnation.

section: I. The Shekinah Glory and Its Significance for Israel
text: The term Logos (Λόγος) — Word — is the precise designation for the eternal Son of God who became flesh. Logos means word, and word means thought. There never was a time when God did not think, and there never was a time when His thought was incomplete. The eternal Logos, the invisible God who dwelt in the Holy of Holies as the Shekinah, became flesh and tabernacled among the Jewish people. The generation of Israel that lived during the ministry of Jesus Christ was therefore the one generation in all of history that looked upon the Shekinah glory with the naked eye. This was the final demonstration to Israel before the nation went out under the fifth cycle of discipline and the times of the Gentiles resumed. The response to that visible manifestation followed the same pattern that had characterized Israel throughout its history: a remnant of positive volition and a majority of negative volition, the remnant according to the election of grace.

section: II. The Doctrine of the Divine Decrees
text: II. The Doctrine of the Divine Decrees

section: A. Definition and Scope
text: A. Definition and Scope

section: A. Definition and Scope
text: The divine decrees are the eternal, holy, wise, and sovereign purpose of God, comprehending at once all things that ever were or will be in their causes, conditions, successions, and relations, and determining their certain future occurrence. More concisely: the decrees are the sum total of God's plan for the human race, anticipated through omniscience in eternity past and fixed at that time.

section: A. Definition and Scope
text: The omniscience of God encompasses two categories of knowledge with respect to human history: actuality — the actual thoughts, decisions, and actions of every person throughout history — and probability or possibility — the alternatives that could have been chosen but were not. Only actuality was fed into the computer of the divine decrees. The probabilities and possibilities remain within the knowledge of God but were never decreed, because they do not constitute what actually occurs in history.

section: A. Definition and Scope
text: The printouts from the computer of divine decrees include election, foreknowledge, and predestination for the believer, and condemnation for the unbeliever. These are not independent sources of information; they are outputs from a single input — omniscience feeding actuality into the decrees.

section: B. The Decrees and Free Will
text: B. The Decrees and Free Will

section: B. The Decrees and Free Will
text: A critical distinction must be maintained: the decree is not the execution of a thought, decision, or action. The omniscience of God anticipated the thought, decision, or action of every free agent, and fed it into the decree. The creature's free will is therefore fully operative — the decree does not compel it. This eliminates both the Supralapsarian error (that God is the direct cause of sinful acts) and the Sublapsarian error (that God is the indirect cause). Omniscience merely knew what free will would do and recorded it.

section: B. The Decrees and Free Will
text: There is therefore no ultimate conflict between the decrees of God and the free will of man, or between divine sovereignty and human volition. The decrees deal only with what will happen, not with what will not occur. God decreed the free acts of moral agents as free, and the acts of necessary agents as necessary. The sinful and the righteous, human good and divine good, are all included — not because God caused them, but because God knew them.

section: B. The Decrees and Free Will
text: All causes and effects, conditions and instrumentalities, events and everything that depends on them were known and decreed. Not the slightest uncertainty exists about even the smallest event. All events are interwoven and interdependent. A single uncertainty at the smallest level would introduce confusion into the entire system.

section: C. The Simultaneous Character of the Decrees
text: C. The Simultaneous Character of the Decrees

section: C. The Simultaneous Character of the Decrees
text: The decrees were not issued sequentially. All of the content of the decrees was placed in the computer simultaneously, in an instant, in eternity past — before time, before space, before any creature existed. Time and space constitute the playing field of history, but the decrees existed long before the playing field was laid out. God invented time through the mechanics of the earth's rotation and orbit; He existed before either.

section: C. The Simultaneous Character of the Decrees
text: Because all things were decreed simultaneously, what is past, present, and future from the human standpoint is equally certain from the divine standpoint. God does not learn; God does not gain in knowledge. Everything that is ever knowable was known instantly, always, from eternity past.

section: III. The Foreknowledge of God
text: III. The Foreknowledge of God

section: A. Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience
text: A. Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience

section: A. Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience
text: Foreknowledge is not synonymous with omniscience, and it is not synonymous with foresight. These are distinct categories of divine knowledge and must not be conflated, particularly in the interpretation of Romans 9 and Romans 11.

section: A. Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience
text: Three categories of divine knowledge are operative in the doctrine of the decrees. First, God's self-knowledge — His perfect, eternal knowledge of Himself — which is the only form of purely subjective divine knowledge, and which precedes any system of decrees. God knew Himself always to exist; there was never a time when He did not. Second, omniscience — God's complete knowledge of all creatures and all events, both actual and probable, possessed in eternity past before any creature existed. Third, foreknowledge — a distinct category that does not exist until the decrees exist.

section: B. Foreknowledge as Cognizance of the Decrees
text: B. Foreknowledge as Cognizance of the Decrees

section: B. Foreknowledge as Cognizance of the Decrees
text: Foreknowledge is not knowledge of future events in the sense of independent advance perception. It is the cognizance of what is already in the divine decrees. Foreknowledge is located at the output end of the computer, not the input end. Omniscience fed reality into the computer; foreknowledge reads the printout.

section: B. Foreknowledge as Cognizance of the Decrees
text: Foreknowledge therefore makes nothing certain. It simply acknowledges what is decreed. No decree ever arises from foreknowledge; causality runs the other direction. Because God decreed all events from His omniscience, He foreknows them as certainly future. Technically, foreknowledge is simultaneous with the decrees, but logically it follows them. To reverse this order — to suggest that foreknowledge precedes and grounds the decrees — would imply that God was not the original cause, which is a blasphemous conclusion. Omniscience precedes the decrees; foreknowledge follows them.

section: B. Foreknowledge as Cognizance of the Decrees
text: Foreknowledge also differs from omniscience in that omniscience includes knowledge of what did not occur — the probabilities and possibilities. Foreknowledge is restricted to what is in the decrees, that is, to actuality. God can display what would have resulted from a probability — a decision that a free agent could have made but did not — but that probability was never part of the decree and is therefore not the object of foreknowledge properly defined.

section: C. The Error of Supralapsarianism
text: C. The Error of Supralapsarianism

section: C. The Error of Supralapsarianism
text: Supralapsarianism teaches that the decree of election and reprobation logically precedes the decree of the fall, making God the direct cause of sin. This is incompatible with the doctrine developed above. Omniscience only decreed what would actually happen; it did not cause the thoughts, decisions, and actions of free agents. Foreknowledge cannot precede the decrees. Since the divine decrees alone establish certainty, nothing can be foreknown until it is first decreed — and what is decreed reflects what omniscience knew as actuality, not a divine causation of evil. The decrees render events certain without rendering God their efficient cause.

section: IV. The Will of God in Relation to the Decrees
text: IV. The Will of God in Relation to the Decrees

section: A. The Eternal Character of the Divine Will
text: A. The Eternal Character of the Divine Will

section: A. The Eternal Character of the Divine Will
text: The will of God is eternal. There never was a time when it did not exist, and there never was a time when it was not totally supreme. The will of God pre-existed time, space, and all creatures. The same will that existed in eternity past in the Father, Son, and Spirit operates in time and space within human history. Because God is immutable, His will is immutable. He cannot be fooled, cannot be caught off guard, and cannot be defeated.

section: A. The Eternal Character of the Divine Will
text: God did not decree Himself to be; He has always existed. Self-knowledge precedes any system of decrees. God knew Himself always to exist, and His self-knowledge is therefore a separate category prior to and independent of the decrees. It is impossible for any member of the Godhead to be corrupted, to make a mistake, to be wrong, to be inconsistent, or to violate one of His own perfect attributes. The justice of God is the guardian of the righteousness of God, and the righteousness of God is the guardian of the justice of God, as justice guards all of the divine attributes.

section: A. The Eternal Character of the Divine Will
text: God is one in essence and three in person. Both the essence and the persons express self-consciousness and self-determination. The will of God must be consistent with His own perfect attributes and His own eternal essence, because immutability and integrity make any compromise of those attributes impossible.

section: B. Four Categories of the Will of God
text: B. Four Categories of the Will of God

section: B. Four Categories of the Will of God
text: Because two categories of rational free will were created — angelic and human — the one eternal will of God must be understood categorically as it functions in relation to those free agents within human history.

section: B. Four Categories of the Will of God
text: First, the directive will of God: God has a specific plan for each individual life, expressed as the X-Y-Z framework of election, foreknowledge, and predestination. This is what God has positively designed and directs toward the believer.

section: B. Four Categories of the Will of God
text: Second, the determined (permissive) will of God: God has permitted non-meritorious volition, allowing the free agent to choose between blessing and cursing. The permissive will is not passive indifference; divine justice deals with negative volition, and the consequences of that dealing are real and significant.

section: B. Four Categories of the Will of God
text: Third, the overruling will of God: God overrules the failures of the creature to accomplish His ultimate purpose without violating the creature's freedom. The glory of God and the pleasure of God will be fulfilled in the function of the human race regardless of any individual's rebellion.

section: B. Four Categories of the Will of God
text: Fourth, the preventative will of God: God has provided doctrine, the laws of divine establishment, the royal family honor code, and where necessary, divine discipline — all to keep the believer within the functional boundaries of God's plan. This is grace operating in the category of preservation.

section: C. The Will of God and the Glory of God
text: C. The Will of God and the Glory of God

section: C. The Will of God and the Glory of God
text: The decrees unite in one all-inclusive final objective: the glory and the pleasure of God. These are two sides of the same reality. God possessed perfect glory in the eternal fellowship of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit before any creature existed. The decrees do not add to or subtract from that glory. When the decrees are completed — when the last event of human history has occurred and the angelic conflict is resolved — God will possess the same perfect glory He had before. The only addition is that certain creatures — elect angels and born-again believers — will be included in that glory on the other side. That inclusion is the grace of God.

section: C. The Will of God and the Glory of God
text: There will be no equality in the eternal state. Freedom guarantees inequality, and the eternal state will reflect the reality that those who advanced to spiritual maturity through consistent doctrine intake will occupy a position of greater blessing and glory than those who were saved but never advanced. This is not a failure of divine justice; it is the expression of it. The highest glorification available to any creature is maturity adjustment to the justice of God.

section: V. The Extent of the Divine Decrees
text: V. The Extent of the Divine Decrees

section: V. The Extent of the Divine Decrees
text: God has decreed ends as well as means, causes as well as effects, conditions as well as instrumentalities. Some things God has decreed to accomplish immediately — creation, for instance. Other things He accomplishes through secondary causes operating under the law of necessity. Still other things He has permitted free agents to do in the exercise of their free will. All three categories of events are equally certain within the computer of the divine decrees.

section: V. The Extent of the Divine Decrees
text: Providence is the system by which God molds all events into the fulfillment of His eternal purpose and pleasure. Preservation continues the existence of things; providence directs their progress. Both are expressions of the divine decrees operating in time and space. The doctrine of logistical grace — God's provision of everything necessary for the believer's physical existence and spiritual function — is the practical face of providence in the individual believer's life.

section: VI. The Primacy of Doctrinal Thought
text: VI. The Primacy of Doctrinal Thought

section: VI. The Primacy of Doctrinal Thought
text: A central implication of the doctrine of the divine decrees for the life of the believer is the absolute primacy of doctrinal thinking. Whatever was fed into the computer of the divine decrees from eternity past included not only the facts of human history but the provision of doctrine — the canon of Scripture — available at every point in that history as the instrument of God's solution to every problem, personal and historical.

section: VI. The Primacy of Doctrinal Thought
text: The omniscience of God knew every problem every believer would ever face, both individually and collectively, billions of years before any of those problems arose. Because God is perfect and His plan is perfect, no problem exists without a perfect solution. That solution is invariably related to doctrine. The believer who has been taking in doctrine consistently possesses the solution in advance of the crisis. The believer who neglects doctrine has no access to the divine solution at the moment of need, regardless of what human alternatives may be tried.

section: VI. The Primacy of Doctrinal Thought
text: This principle has collective as well as individual application. A pivot of mature believers in a national entity — those who have advanced to maturity adjustment to the justice of God through consistent doctrine intake — constitutes the only real stabilizing force in any historical crisis. National disasters, the decline of client-nation status, the advance of tyranny — all of these move according to the divine decrees. The response available to the believer is not political but doctrinal: maximum intake of Bible doctrine on a consistent daily basis, from which position the individual believer and the corporate pivot become the means by which Jesus Christ controls history.

section: VI. The Primacy of Doctrinal Thought
text: The principle of Alpha and Omega is relevant here. The believer, caught between the beginning and the end of history, has access to the One who knows the end from the beginning. The will of God in eternity past, which knew every thought, decision, and action in advance, is the same will that operates in the present moment. The solution was available before the problem existed. The believer reaches back to the eternal will and forward to the certain consummation — the Rapture of the Church, the Tribulation, the Second Advent, and the Millennium — through the one instrument that bridges the gap: the daily intake of Bible doctrine under the teaching ministry of God the Holy Spirit through the Grace Apparatus for Perception.

section: VI. The Primacy of Doctrinal Thought
text: Thought is primary; action is derivative. The greatest human beings in history are those who have advanced furthest in doctrinal thinking. Paul is the paradigm case: his singular contribution to humanity was not his missionary activity or his personal suffering, though both were real, but the depth and precision of his doctrinal thought. That thought was possible because he had doctrine — maximum doctrine, consistently received and metabolized into epignosis.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy-Four
text: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy-Four

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy-Four
text: 1. The Shekinah glory was the visible manifestation of the preincarnate Christ, present with Israel throughout its history. Dwelling between the cherubim in the Holy of Holies, restricted behind the veil, the Shekinah was accessible only through the annual high-priestly ritual of the Day of Atonement. The incarnation was the moment when the Shekinah glory became visible to the entire nation. That one generation saw what no prior generation had seen directly, and their response followed the pattern of all prior generations: negative volition in the majority, a remnant according to the election of grace.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy-Four
text: 2. The divine decrees are the eternal, immutable record of everything that will actually occur in history — thought, decision, and action — fed into the computer of God's plan from His omniscience in eternity past. The decrees are simultaneous, comprehensive, and certain. They include the free acts of moral agents as free and the acts of necessary agents as necessary. God is not the cause of sinful acts recorded in the decrees; omniscience anticipated and recorded them without producing them.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy-Four
text: 3. Omniscience, the decrees, and foreknowledge are three distinct categories that must not be conflated. Omniscience precedes the decrees logically and feeds actuality — not probability — into them. Foreknowledge is a printout from the decrees, not an input to them. Foreknowledge makes nothing certain; it acknowledges what is already certain by virtue of the decree. No decree arises from foreknowledge. To reverse this order is to imply that God was not the original cause — a theological error that misreads Romans 9 and Romans 11.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy-Four
text: 4. The free will of man is fully compatible with the divine decrees. The decrees do not compel or override human volition. Omniscience knew what every free agent would think, decide, and do, and recorded it. The creature's choice remains genuinely free; the decree renders it certain without causing it. This rules out both Supralapsarian determinism (God as direct cause of sin) and any form of fatalism.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy-Four
text: 5. The will of God is eternal, immutable, and operates in four categorical modes within human history. The directive will designs a positive plan for the believer. The permissive will allows negative volition while permitting divine justice to respond to it. The overruling will ensures that God's ultimate purpose is accomplished regardless of creature failure. The preventative will provides doctrine, the laws of divine establishment, and divine discipline to keep the believer within the functional boundaries of grace. All four modes are expressions of one eternal will.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy-Four
text: 6. The highest glorification available to any creature is maturity adjustment to the justice of God. The decrees unite in one final objective: the glory and pleasure of God. Creatures are included in that glory only by grace. The degree of their participation is determined by their advance toward spiritual maturity. Freedom guarantees inequality in outcome; the eternal state will reflect the reality of that inequality. There is no equality in the eternal state — only the freedom, fully exercised or neglected, that produced differentiated results.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy-Four
text: 7. Doctrinal thinking is the primary category of the Christian life; action is derivative. Because omniscience knew every problem in advance and fed the solution — Bible doctrine — into the decrees, the believer who takes in doctrine consistently possesses the divine solution before the crisis arrives. No crisis, personal or historical, exists without a perfect solution in the plan of God. That solution is accessed exclusively through the daily, consistent intake and metabolization of Bible doctrine. The pivot of mature believers is the only stabilizing force in a nation facing historical judgment.

section: Glossary
text: The body of mature believers in a national entity whose maturity adjustment to the justice of God sustains divine blessing on that nation and delays or prevents divine judgment. The pivot is the primary stabilizing force in any national historical crisis. Its existence or absence determines the course of national history under the five cycles of discipline.

section: Glossary
text: Epignosis

section: Glossary
text: ἐπίγνωσις epignōsis — full, exact knowledge

section: Glossary
text: The category of knowledge required for spiritual growth, distinguished from gnosis (academic knowledge). Epignosis is Bible doctrine metabolized under the teaching ministry of God the Holy Spirit through the Grace Apparatus for Perception and transferred from the left lobe to the right lobe, where it becomes operational in the believer's thinking and decision-making.

section: Glossary
text: Five cycles of discipline

section: Glossary
text: Progressive stages of national divine discipline as outlined in Leviticus 26, applied to client nations that reject the laws of divine establishment and the divine protocol. The fifth cycle constitutes complete historical destruction — military conquest and the end of the nation's client status. Israel went out under the fifth cycle with the fall of Jerusalem in AD 70; Gentile client nations face the same pattern under the times of the Gentiles.

section: Glossary
text: Logistical grace

section: Glossary
text: God's provision of everything necessary for the believer's physical existence and spiritual function throughout the course of the Christian life. Logistical grace is the practical expression of providence operating in the individual believer's life, guaranteeing that no believer ever lacks what is needed to execute the protocol plan of God.

section: Romans 9:10 — The Perfect Plan of God: Decrees, Election, Predestination, and the Integrity of God
text: Romans 9:10 — The Perfect Plan of God: Decrees, Election, Predestination, and the Integrity of God

section: Romans 9:10 — The Perfect Plan of God: Decrees, Election, Predestination, and the Integrity of God
text: Romans 9:10 “And not only so, but also when Rebekah had conceived children by one man, our forefather Isaac...” (ESV)

section: Romans 9:10 — The Perfect Plan of God: Decrees, Election, Predestination, and the Integrity of God
text: Corrected translation: And not only this, but also when Rebekah had conceived children by one man, our ancestor Isaac...

section: Romans 9:10 — The Perfect Plan of God: Decrees, Election, Predestination, and the Integrity of God
text: Romans 9 continues Paul's extended treatment of Israel's place within the sovereign plan of God. Having established in the preceding verses that physical descent from Abraham does not constitute membership in the true Israel, Paul turns to the case of Isaac and Rebekah to press the point further. Before resuming the exegesis of verse 10, the present chapter develops the doctrinal substructure that underlies the passage: the perfect plan of God, the divine decrees, the seven imputations, the categories of election and predestination, and the integrity of God as the mechanism through which all divine blessing flows to imperfect creatures.

section: I. The Perfect Plan of God and the Glory of God
text: I. The Perfect Plan of God and the Glory of God

section: I. The Perfect Plan of God and the Glory of God
text: The divine decrees unite in one all-inclusive final objective: the glory of God. Before any creature existed — in Alpha eternity — God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Spirit coexisted with identical, perfect, and immutable attributes. They possessed not only glory but pleasure. On the other side of time, in Omega eternity, that glory remains unchanged and undiminished. Nothing that occurs within history detracts from the glory of God. The plan of God cannot be hindered; a creature may align with it or be overrun by it, but cannot alter it.

section: I. The Perfect Plan of God and the Glory of God
text: Because God is alone before all creation, the decrees concern no one but the members of the Trinity. Rational volition was placed into angelic and human creatures within time, and God knew with perfect precision how each free agent would think, decide, and act. He originated the capacity for volition but bears no responsibility for the decisions made within it. Supralapsarianism — the view that God decreed the fall and sin as positive ends — is inconsistent with the biblical data. God is not the author of sin. Adam's sin arose from Adam's own free will, and both sin and the cross were known to omniscience and fed into the computer of the divine decrees as actualities.

section: I. The Perfect Plan of God and the Glory of God
text: Being eternal and infinite, the three persons of the Trinity are worthy of glory. God's glory is what He is in His essence and in His person. It follows logically that God will be glorified in what He is and in what He has decreed. The manifestation of His glory secures the highest good for His creatures: a maturity adjustment to the justice of God and the resultant blessing that flows from it. God is pleased and glorified both in the believer's momentum through the plan of God and in the believer's advance from salvation adjustment through maturity adjustment.

section: II. The Seven Imputations and the Tactical Victory of the Angelic Conflict
text: II. The Seven Imputations and the Tactical Victory of the Angelic Conflict

section: II. The Seven Imputations and the Tactical Victory of the Angelic Conflict
text: The divine decrees are executed through imputations from the justice of God. The entire plan of God is structured on the doctrine of divine imputation. Seven imputations constitute the tactical victory of the angelic conflict, glorifying God in both time and eternity.

section: A. The First Two Imputations: Real Imputations at Birth
text: A. The First Two Imputations: Real Imputations at Birth

section: A. The First Two Imputations: Real Imputations at Birth
text: The first real imputation is human life imputed to its divinely prepared target, the human soul. There is affinity between human life and the human soul; once imputed, that life is permanent and cannot be removed. The second real imputation is Adam's original sin imputed to the genetically formed old sin nature. Every member of the human race is condemned by one sin — Adam's sin — not by personal sins. Personal sins are neither the ground of condemnation nor individually judged at the bar of divine justice during the believer's lifetime; they are collected and reserved for a single judicial transaction.

section: B. The Third Imputation: Judicial Imputation at the Cross
text: B. The Third Imputation: Judicial Imputation at the Cross

section: B. The Third Imputation: Judicial Imputation at the Cross
text: All personal sins of the entire human race — past, present, and future — were imputed to Christ on the cross. This is a judicial imputation involving only one factor: personal sins. Real imputations have two factors (an entity imputed and a prepared home with which it has affinity); judicial imputations have only one factor and no such affinity requirement. The cross is therefore the indispensable basis for salvation adjustment to the justice of God.

section: C. The Fourth and Fifth Imputations: Salvation Adjustment
text: C. The Fourth and Fifth Imputations: Salvation Adjustment

section: C. The Fourth and Fifth Imputations: Salvation Adjustment
text: At the moment of faith in Christ, two further imputations occur. First, the justice of God imputes His perfect righteousness to the believer — a judicial imputation. There is no affinity involved; the justice of God credits the believer with what the believer does not possess by nature. Second, eternal life is imputed to its divinely prepared home: the human spirit, which God the Holy Spirit creates instantaneously at the moment of salvation. This is regeneration — to be born again means that the Holy Spirit creates a human spirit and eternal life is imputed to it. The believer therefore possesses both a soul (containing human life) and a human spirit (containing eternal life).

section: D. The Sixth and Seventh Imputations: Maturity and Eternity
text: D. The Sixth and Seventh Imputations: Maturity and Eternity

section: D. The Sixth and Seventh Imputations: Maturity and Eternity
text: Blessing in time is imputed to its divinely prepared home: the imputed righteousness of God resident in the believer. All divine blessing must pass through the grace pipeline to the righteousness of God. If God were to bless on any other basis, His attributes would be compromised and He would cease to be God. This is the sixth imputation and it constitutes the reward for maturity adjustment to the justice of God.

section: D. The Sixth and Seventh Imputations: Maturity and Eternity
text: Blessing in eternity — eternal reward — is imputed as a real imputation to its divinely prepared home: the resurrection body. This seventh imputation glorifies God forever in Omega eternity. Each imputation is parlayed into the next, forming the structure of the plan of God in equation form.

section: III. The X-Y-Z Equation of the Plan of God
text: III. The X-Y-Z Equation of the Plan of God

section: III. The X-Y-Z Equation of the Plan of God
text: The plan of God may be expressed as a three-stage equation. In the X-radical, human life is imputed at physical birth; Adam's original sin immediately follows, condemning the individual and establishing the potential for salvation. Condemnation must precede salvation. The pertinent doctrine at this stage is the gospel, and the first hope — absolute confidence in Christ — results in salvation adjustment to the justice of God through faith in the Lord Jesus Christ.

section: III. The X-Y-Z Equation of the Plan of God
text: In the Y-radical, the two judicial imputations — personal sins to Christ at the cross, and God's righteousness to the believer at salvation — are balanced. The second judicial imputation establishes the potential for great blessing in time. Sustained intake of doctrine produces the second hope: absolute confidence that persisting in the perception of doctrine leads to maturity adjustment to the justice of God through maximum doctrine resident in the soul.

section: III. The X-Y-Z Equation of the Plan of God
text: In the Z-radical, eternal life imputed at salvation and blessing in time imputed at maturity together establish the potential for blessing in eternity. Undeserved suffering during the prosperity phase focuses the mature believer on Omega eternity. The third hope is absolute confidence that at the judgment seat of Christ the seventh imputation — eternal blessing in the resurrection body — glorifies God forever.

section: IV. The Racial Origin of Israel in Relation to the Plan of God
text: IV. The Racial Origin of Israel in Relation to the Plan of God

section: IV. The Racial Origin of Israel in Relation to the Plan of God
text: All Gentile races originate in the X-radical through physical birth. All Gentiles descend from Shem, Ham, or Japheth, the three sons of Noah. The Jewish race, by contrast, originated in the Z-radical. Abraham was approximately ninety-nine years of age — a Sumero-Akkadian Gentile who had achieved both salvation and maturity adjustment to the justice of God — when God constituted him the father of the Jewish race. The Jewish race is unique in all of human history as the only race formed on the basis of regeneration and maturity adjustment.

section: IV. The Racial Origin of Israel in Relation to the Plan of God
text: Abraham had eight sons, but only Isaac perpetuated the racial and spiritual line, because Isaac likewise attained both salvation and maturity adjustment. Isaac's son Jacob, though his twin Esau held the right of primogeniture, was the heir of the line because Esau remained in the X-radical as an unbeliever, while Jacob advanced through the plan of God to both salvation and maturity adjustment. The line of Israel therefore runs from Abraham to Isaac to Jacob — which is why the Lord Jesus Christ, the Shekinah glory, is called the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Anyone who carries the genes of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob is a racial Jew — the physical seed of Abraham. Paul's burden throughout Romans 9 is that being the physical seed is insufficient; the true Jew must also be the spiritual seed of Abraham, which requires advancing from the X-radical into the Y and Z-radicals.

section: IV. The Racial Origin of Israel in Relation to the Plan of God
text: Paul writes at the end of a generation that had witnessed the Shekinah glory made visible in the hypostatic union. The Shekinah glory, identified by John as the Logos, became flesh and tabernacled among them. The same grace principle applies: it is not sight of God that determines spiritual outcome, but volition toward the doctrine that presents God. Positive volition toward Christ at salvation and positive volition toward doctrine thereafter — these are the conditions for every advance in the plan of God.

section: V. Omniscience, Foreknowledge, and the Divine Decrees
text: V. Omniscience, Foreknowledge, and the Divine Decrees

section: V. Omniscience, Foreknowledge, and the Divine Decrees
text: The omniscience of God, in Alpha eternity, knew every thought, every decision, and every action that would ever occur throughout all of history. These are the actualities — the realities — and they alone were fed into the computer of the divine decrees. Possibilities and probabilities — alternatives to what actually happened — were known to omniscience but were not incorporated into the decrees.

section: V. Omniscience, Foreknowledge, and the Divine Decrees
text: Foreknowledge is not identical with omniscience and must be carefully distinguished from it. Foreknowledge does not precede the decrees; it does not constitute knowing something in advance as a basis for the decrees. Rather, foreknowledge merely acknowledges what is already in the decrees. Omniscience feeds the computer; foreknowledge is the printout. Omniscience knows both the actual and the potential; foreknowledge knows only what is decreed.

section: V. Omniscience, Foreknowledge, and the Divine Decrees
text: A third category is divine self-knowledge, which is distinct from both omniscience (knowledge of all things outside God) and foreknowledge (acknowledgment of what is decreed). God in His omniscience knew, in eternity past, what thoughts, motives, and decisions would carry one believer to maturity and another into reversionism. The plan is thus consistent with human volition and freedom at every point. God is the inventor of freedom and does not tamper with His own invention. A distinction must be maintained between what God causes directly — supremely, the cross — and what God permits indirectly, such as sin, human good, and evil.

section: VI. Election
text: VI. Election

section: VI. Election
text: Election is a printout from the computer of the divine decrees. God's omniscience fed into the decrees every thought, decision, and action that would occur in history, and one category of that printout concerns believers: this is election. Election is that part of the decrees dealing with the thoughts, decisions, and actions of believers who are related to the plan of God beyond the X-radical.

section: VI. Election
text: There are two levels of election: individual and collective. Individual election designates each believer as called and elect. Collective election designates bodies of believers assembled for a special divine purpose. Israel is a collective election, formed so that a Jewish nation could exist at the time of the Exodus. That nation — Yisra'el — was the first client nation in history, functioning under the Mosaic law with the responsibilities of evangelism, growth in grace, and missionary activity. The church is a separate collective election — the royal family of God — encompassing believing Jews and Gentiles in union with Christ during the Church Age. Millennial saints constitute a further distinct election.

section: VI. Election
text: The times of the Gentiles — the period from 70 AD until the Second Advent — is the interval during which only a Gentile nation can function as a client nation to God. During the Tribulation, which belongs to the Jewish age, 144,000 individual Jews serve in place of a client nation. At the Second Advent, Israel is restored to that function by Christ. All these categories are printouts from the same decrees. There is no overflow from one election to another. Election is exclusively a term applied to believers; it is never used of unbelievers.

section: VI. Election
text: Christ Himself is the primary individual election, as Isaiah 42:1 makes clear: 'Behold My servant whom I uphold, My chosen one in whom My soul delights.' The election of the church is grounded in union with Christ; believers share His elected status by virtue of their position in Him (Ephesians 1:3–6; 2 Thessalonians 2:13; Titus 1:1; 1 Peter 2:4–6).

section: VII. Predestination, Foreordination, and Predetermination
text: VII. Predestination, Foreordination, and Predetermination

section: VII. Predestination, Foreordination, and Predetermination
text: Three terms in the New Testament — predestination, foreordination, and predetermination — are closely related and apply exclusively to believers. They are never used of unbelievers. There is no biblical statement that any unbeliever is predestined, foreordained, or predetermined to hell. Unbelievers go to the lake of fire through their own self-determination — by exercising their free will to reject Christ at God-consciousness, at gospel hearing, and throughout their lives. The words predestination, foreordination, and predetermination are printout vocabulary for believers only.

section: VII. Predestination, Foreordination, and Predetermination
text: The Hegelian pattern — thesis produces antithesis, antithesis combines with thesis to produce synthesis — does not apply to biblical revelation. The Scripture states what it states; where there is no antithesis given, none may be supplied by logical inference. The thesis 'the believer is predestined to eternal life' is true. The proposed antithesis 'therefore the unbeliever is predestined to hell' has no scriptural warrant and contradicts the consistent biblical teaching on human free will. This error has marred the reception of Reformed soteriology for generations.

section: VII. Predestination, Foreordination, and Predetermination
text: Foreordination — the Greek noun prothesis (πρόθεσις) and verb proorizō (προορίζω) — designates God's preconceived and predesigned plan for the believer. It is synonymous with the decrees, with specific emphasis on logistical grace: God not only decreed that there would be believers, but decreed the full logistical support required to bring each believer through the plan of God. There is no difficulty in life — no adversity, no tragedy, no trial personal or collective — for which the decrees do not already contain perfect provision.

section: VII. Predestination, Foreordination, and Predetermination
text: Predetermination — the Greek verb protithēmi (προτίθημι) — emphasizes the provision side: God fed into the decrees not only the facts about believers but the entire logistical apparatus by which they would be supported. Doctrine at the right time, in the right place; every resource of logistical grace. Predestination, the most common of the three terms, refers to the permanent relation of the believer in Christ to the plan of God through positional truth. For the royal family of God in the Church Age, predestination means precisely this: we share the destiny of Christ. At salvation the Holy Spirit enters the believer into union with Christ; since Christ is the elected, foreordained, and predestined one, the believer shares His eternal destiny.

section: VII. Predestination, Foreordination, and Predetermination
text: The Father predetermined the grace concept of propitiation (Romans 3:25), so that election, foreknowledge, and predestination would always be printouts from the decrees in connection with believers related to Christ. The divine decrees are therefore the sum of the facts fed into the computer of omniscience plus the full logistical support provided for every believer — and predestination, election, and foreknowledge are the principal printout categories pertaining to believers.

section: VIII. The Integrity of God: Righteousness, Justice, and the Love of God
text: VIII. The Integrity of God: Righteousness, Justice, and the Love of God

section: VIII. The Integrity of God: Righteousness, Justice, and the Love of God
text: The integrity of God is that component of His essence which combines two attributes: perfect righteousness and divine justice. In Scripture these two together are called holiness. Righteousness is God's internal standard; justice is His external administration of that standard toward creatures. Justice is mankind's point of reference in relation to God. The entire Epistle to the Romans is a dissertation on the righteousness of God and its related justification — demonstrating how a perfect God can provide a perfect plan for imperfect persons by supplying, at salvation, His own perfect righteousness.

section: A. The Divine Attribute of Love
text: A. The Divine Attribute of Love

section: A. The Divine Attribute of Love
text: Understanding the integrity of God requires first understanding the love of God as a divine attribute — which is fundamentally unlike human love at every point.

section: A. The Divine Attribute of Love
text: First: God's love is complete and total, eternally existing as a component of His being, without reference to any object. In Alpha eternity, before the decrees, God's love was complete and total. In Omega eternity, after history is over, God's love will be complete and total. God does not fall in love. Falling in love is a human process requiring the prior development of capacity — the maturation of norms and standards in the soul. God possesses perfect love eternally without ever requiring an object. His love is not generated by an object, is not maintained by emotional stimulation, and is not in any degree sustained by emotion. It exists at the same degree of intensity eternally, unaffected by the existence or non-existence of any creature.

section: A. The Divine Attribute of Love
text: Second: there are two known objects of God's love, and both have always existed. The first is God's own perfect righteousness — internal and subjective. God the Father has always loved His own righteousness; there was never a time when He did not. The second is the other persons of the Trinity — external and objective. The Father loves the Son and the Spirit; the Son loves the Father and the Spirit; the Spirit loves the Father and the Son, with that same eternal, immutable, non-emotional perfect love. Both objects of divine love are eternal; they were never acquired and cannot change.

section: A. The Divine Attribute of Love
text: Third: in righteousness, God's love for holiness — for integrity — is revealed. In justice, God's hatred for sin, human good, and evil is revealed. These two attributes of the divine integrity operate together. Righteousness identifies what God loves and what He cannot accept; justice executes the verdict that righteousness demands.

section: B. The Exclusion of Creatures from the Divine Attribute of Love
text: B. The Exclusion of Creatures from the Divine Attribute of Love

section: B. The Exclusion of Creatures from the Divine Attribute of Love
text: All creatures are excluded from the divine attribute of love because of three facts: Adam's original sin imputed at birth; the old sin nature formed genetically in every member of the human race; and the personal manifestations of the old sin nature — personal sins, human good, and evil. God's righteousness loves His own righteousness and cannot accept Adam's original sin, the old sin nature, or anything the old sin nature produces. God's justice condemns each of these in turn.

section: B. The Exclusion of Creatures from the Divine Attribute of Love
text: This means that John 3:16 — 'God so loved the world' — cannot be referring to the divine attribute of love in its technical sense. The statement is an anthropopathism: an ascription to God, in human terms, of a response that does not correspond to an actual divine attribute but communicates a truth about God's attitude toward mankind in a form human beings can apprehend. Similarly, the statement in Genesis that 'the Lord repented that He had made man' is an anthropopathism. God does not repent; He fed everything into the decrees. Such expressions communicate divine responses in human emotional vocabulary without implying that God has emotions in the human sense.

section: B. The Exclusion of Creatures from the Divine Attribute of Love
text: The love of God, as a divine attribute, stops at His own righteousness. His righteousness says it cannot accept sin, the old sin nature, or its products; His justice condemns them. That would be the end — except that the justice of God, acting consistently with the righteousness of God, is also the agent of salvation. God imputes His righteousness to the believer judicially at the moment of faith in Christ. The believer now possesses the righteousness of God. And God loves His own righteousness wherever it resides. Now God loves the believer — not for what the believer is in himself, but because the believer possesses the righteousness of God. This is the central mechanism of Romans: a perfect God blessing imperfect persons by providing them with His own perfect righteousness as the target of His imputed blessings.

section: B. The Exclusion of Creatures from the Divine Attribute of Love
text: Without the righteousness of God, nothing in a creature constitutes a basis for divine love or divine blessing. Human good, moral effort, and religious observance — whether individual or institutional — provide no such basis. They are products of the old sin nature operating in the moral sphere and are as unacceptable to divine righteousness as overt sins. The only foundation for blessing from the justice of God is the righteousness of God, imputed at salvation and resident in the believer.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy-Five
text: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy-Five

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy-Five
text: 1. The final objective of the divine decrees is the glory of God. All of history — angelic and human — is encompassed in decrees that unite in one all-inclusive purpose: the glorification of the triune God. Nothing in the decrees detracts from that glory; creatures may align with the plan or be overrun by it, but cannot alter it.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy-Five
text: 2. Only actualities enter the divine decrees. Omniscience in Alpha eternity knew every thought, decision, and action of every free agent. Only these realities were incorporated into the decrees. Possibilities and probabilities were known to omniscience but were not decreed. Foreknowledge is not identical with omniscience; it is the acknowledgment of what omniscience has already placed in the decrees.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy-Five
text: 3. The seven imputations constitute the tactical victory of the angelic conflict. Two real imputations at birth (human life to the soul; Adam's sin to the old sin nature), one judicial imputation at the cross (all personal sins to Christ), two imputations at salvation (God's righteousness judicially; eternal life to the human spirit), one imputation at maturity (temporal blessing to God's righteousness), and one imputation at the resurrection (eternal blessing to the resurrection body) — these seven together form the complete structure of divine provision in history.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy-Five
text: 4. The Jewish race is unique in originating from the Z-radical. All Gentile races originate in the X-radical through physical birth. The Jewish race originated when Abraham, at the threshold of maturity adjustment to the justice of God, was constituted the father of a new race. The line was perpetuated through Isaac and Jacob on the same basis: salvation and maturity adjustment. Paul's burden in Romans 9 is that racial descent from Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob (the physical seed) is not sufficient — one must also be the spiritual seed, which requires personal advance through the plan of God.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy-Five
text: 5. Election, foreknowledge, and predestination are printout vocabulary for believers only. These terms designate categories within the divine decrees that pertain exclusively to those who believe in Christ. They are never applied to unbelievers in Scripture. Reprobation, condemnation, and judgment are the corresponding terms for the unbeliever's end — which is reached not by divine predetermination but by the unbeliever's own self-determination in rejecting Christ.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy-Five
text: 6. No one is predestined to hell. The inference that, since believers are predestined to eternal life, unbelievers must be predestined to hell has no scriptural warrant. It substitutes Hegelian dialectic for biblical statement. The unbeliever goes to the lake of fire because he exercises his own free will to say no at God-consciousness and at gospel hearing. The hardening of Pharaoh's heart illustrates the principle: God extended Pharaoh's life and multiplied his opportunities to respond, and Pharaoh accumulated a sustained negative-volition record through his own choices.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy-Five
text: 7. The integrity of God — righteousness plus justice — is the mechanism of all divine blessing. God's perfect righteousness sets the standard; God's justice administers that standard toward creatures. Because all creatures are born with Adam's imputed sin, a functioning old sin nature, and the products of the old sin nature, they are excluded from the divine attribute of love in its technical sense. The solution is not God relaxing His standard but God supplying what His standard requires: His own righteousness imputed to the believer at salvation. Once the believer possesses God's righteousness, God loves the believer — not for what the believer is in himself, but because the believer possesses what God loves.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy-Five
text: 8. The divine attribute of love is totally devoid of emotion. God does not fall in love, does not maintain love through emotional stimulation, and does not require an object in order to possess love. His love is complete, eternal, immutable, and non-emotional. Most biblical references to God loving human beings employ the anthropopathism — an ascription of human emotional response to God for the purpose of communicating a truth in terms human beings can receive. The anthropopathism of divine love will be taken up in detail in the following chapter.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy-Five
text: 9. All blessing from God flows through divine justice to divine righteousness. God cannot bless on any other basis without compromising His attributes. Human effort, moral performance, religious observance, and human good are products of the old sin nature and are no more acceptable to divine righteousness than overt sin. The grace pipeline runs exclusively from the justice of God to the righteousness of God imputed to the believer — and from there to every category of divine blessing in time and eternity.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Seventy-Five
text: 10. The plan of God is consistent with human volition at every point. God is the author of freedom and the inventor of human volition. He does not coerce decisions, override self-determination, or tamper with the volition He created. The distinction between what God causes directly (e.g., the cross) and what God permits indirectly (e.g., sin) is essential to a correct understanding of the decrees and preserves both divine sovereignty and human freedom without collapsing either into the other.

text: The central subject of the Epistle to the Romans. The perfect righteousness that belongs to God as a component of His essence and that is imputed judicially to the believer at salvation. The target of all divine blessing; without it no creature can receive anything from the justice of God.

section: Glossary
text: anthropopathism

section: Glossary
text: anthropopathismos — ascription of human emotion to God

section: Glossary
text: A figure of speech in which a human emotional response is ascribed to God for the purpose of communicating a divine truth in terms accessible to human comprehension. God does not possess emotions in the human sense; anthropopathisms accommodate the infinite to the finite without implying that God is subject to emotional states. 'God so loved the world' (John 3:16) and 'the Lord repented' (Genesis 6:6) are examples.

section: Glossary
text: hypostatic union

section: Glossary
text: hypostatikē henōsis

section: Glossary
text: The permanent union of full deity and true humanity in the one person of Jesus Christ. The Shekinah glory — the visible manifestation of the second person of the Trinity — became flesh and tabernacled among men (John 1:14) in the only form in which the invisible God could be seen: the God-man.

section: Glossary
text: logistical grace

section: Glossary
text: God's provision of everything necessary for the believer's continued physical existence and spiritual advance in time. Incorporated into the divine decrees as part of foreordination: God decreed not only that there would be believers but that they would be fully supplied with every resource needed to execute the plan of God.

section: Glossary
text: old sin nature (OSN)

section: Glossary
text: The sin capacity formed genetically in every member of the human race through the male genetic line. Adam's original sin is imputed to it at birth. It is the source of personal sins, human good, and evil — all of which are unacceptable to the righteousness of God and condemned by the justice of God.

section: Glossary
text: client nation

section: Glossary
text: A national entity that fulfills specific divine purposes in a given dispensation: maintaining freedom under the laws of divine establishment, supporting Bible teaching, conducting evangelism, and providing a base for missionary activity. Israel was the first client nation; during the times of the Gentiles (70 AD to the Second Advent), only Gentile nations can serve in this role.

section: Glossary
text: supralapsarianism

section: Glossary
text: supralapsarianismos

section: Glossary
text: The theological position that God decreed the fall and the damnation of the reprobate as positive ends prior to and independent of His decree to create. Rejected by the present commentary as inconsistent with the biblical data: God is not the author of sin; human self-determination is the cause of sin; and no unbeliever is predestined or foreordained to hell.

section: Glossary

section: Glossary
text: The third category of adjustment to the justice of God, achieved through sustained daily intake of Bible doctrine over time. Culminates in the believer cracking the maturity barrier and advancing to supergrace and ultra-supergrace, at which point the sixth imputation — temporal blessing to the righteousness of God — is activated.
