section: Romans 9:14 — Divine Decrees: Mechanics and Characteristics; Election, Foreknowledge, Predestination; Thanksgiving as Capacity for Life
text: Romans 9:14 — Divine Decrees: Mechanics and Characteristics; Election, Foreknowledge, Predestination; Thanksgiving as Capacity for Life

section: Romans 9:14 — Divine Decrees: Mechanics and Characteristics; Election, Foreknowledge, Predestination; Thanksgiving as Capacity for Life
text: Romans 9:14 “What shall we say then? Is there injustice on God's part? By no means!” (ESV)

section: Romans 9:14 — Divine Decrees: Mechanics and Characteristics; Election, Foreknowledge, Predestination; Thanksgiving as Capacity for Life
text: Corrected translation: What therefore shall we say? Is there unrighteousness with God? Absolutely not!

section: Romans 9:14 — Divine Decrees: Mechanics and Characteristics; Election, Foreknowledge, Predestination; Thanksgiving as Capacity for Life
text: Romans 9:14 stands at the pivot of Paul's extended argument concerning divine election and the integrity of God's promises to Israel. Having established in verses 6–13 that God's elective purpose has always operated through spiritual rather than physical lineage — from Abraham through Isaac and Jacob rather than through Ishmael or Esau — Paul now faces the sharpest possible objection: does this pattern of divine selection constitute injustice? The answer requires a thorough exposition of the doctrine of divine decrees, the mechanics of divine omniscience, and the precise relationship between election, foreknowledge, and predestination. This chapter develops those mechanics in preparation for the exegesis of verses 14–18, while grounding the entire discussion in the believer's capacity for thanksgiving — which is itself a function of maturity adjustment to the justice of God.

section: I. Thanksgiving as Capacity for Life
text: I. Thanksgiving as Capacity for Life

section: I. Thanksgiving as Capacity for Life
text: Thanksgiving is not a seasonal sentiment but a permanent mental attitude belonging to the mature believer. It is inseparable from Bible doctrine resident in the soul. Without doctrine, thanksgiving has no content beyond superficial human gratitude. With maximum doctrine in the right lobe, thanksgiving becomes a total appreciation of everything that life offers within the framework of the Protocol Plan of God.

section: I. Thanksgiving as Capacity for Life
text: The Scriptural foundation for this principle is broad. Ephesians 5:20 commands believers to be thankful for all things in the sphere of the Lord Jesus Christ, directing thanksgiving to God the Father through the person of Christ. 1 Thessalonians 5:18 reinforces this: in everything give thanks, for this is God's will in Christ Jesus. Thanksgiving directed toward God is therefore not optional for the royal family of God — it is the expression of a properly ordered soul.

section: I. Thanksgiving as Capacity for Life
text: Psalm 100:3–5 sets this in its historical context: 'Know that the Lord Himself is God. It is He who made us, and His we are; we are His people and the sheep of His pasture.' The imagery of sheep signals total dependence on the provision of the shepherd. Verse 5 grounds this in the unchanging character of God: His goodness is absolute, His grace is everlasting, His faithfulness extends to all generations. In every generation the key is maturity adjustment to the justice of God.

section: Thanksgiving as a Priestly Function
text: Thanksgiving as a Priestly Function

section: Thanksgiving as a Priestly Function
text: In the Old Testament, the sacrifice of thanksgiving was a specific priestly function. Psalm 116:17 declares, 'To You I shall offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving and call upon the name of the Lord.' Psalm 107:22 calls the Levitical priesthood to offer sacrifices of thanksgiving and recount His works with joyful singing. Amos 4:5 likewise associates the thanksgiving offering with the expression of devotion to the Lord.

section: Thanksgiving as a Priestly Function
text: The transition from the Levitical to the royal priesthood changes the officiant, not the function. Hebrews 13:15 states: 'Through Him, therefore, let us continually offer up a sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of lips that acknowledge His name.' Every Church Age believer, as a member of the royal family of God and a royal priest, is now personally responsible for this sacrifice. The fruit of lips that acknowledge His name is impossible apart from doctrine resident in the soul.

section: Thanksgiving and Imputed Blessing
text: Thanksgiving and Imputed Blessing

section: Thanksgiving and Imputed Blessing
text: Colossians 3:15 draws the connection between thanksgiving and the imputation of blessing at maturity: 'And the blessing and prosperity from Christ — may it be caused to preside in your right lobes — into which supergrace blessings you have also been elected into one body; therefore keep on becoming thankful ones.' The blessing imputed at the maturity barrier presides in the right lobe. That same blessing is described as the very content of election. Thanksgiving is therefore inseparable from election, and election is inseparable from doctrine.

section: Thanksgiving and Imputed Blessing
text: 2 Corinthians 4:15 extends this perspective to history: 'For all things are for your sakes, so that grace, being multiplied to more and more people, may cause the giving of thanks to abound to the glory of God.' The multiplication of grace through Bible teaching produces thanksgiving — and that thanksgiving redounds to the glory of God. This is the purpose toward which the ministry of the Word is directed in every generation.

section: Thanksgiving and Imputed Blessing
text: Colossians 2:7 frames the progression: 'Having been rooted and constantly being edified in Him, constantly being stabilized by means of doctrine resident in the soul in the manner you have been taught, overflowing in thanksgiving.' The overflow of thanksgiving is the natural product of a soul saturated with doctrine. Daniel 2:23, John 11:41, Romans 1:8, 1 Corinthians 1:4, Philippians 1:3, and 2 Timothy 1:3 all record mature believers in the act of thanksgiving — each instance grounded not in circumstance but in the doctrine resident in the soul.

section: II. The Doctrine of Divine Decrees: Definition and Overview
text: II. The Doctrine of Divine Decrees: Definition and Overview

section: II. The Doctrine of Divine Decrees: Definition and Overview
text: The exegesis of Romans 9:14–18 requires a working command of the doctrine of divine decrees. Without this doctrinal framework, the assertion that God 'hated Esau' and 'hardened Pharaoh's heart' inevitably produces the very objection Paul raises and answers: Is there unrighteousness with God?

section: II. The Doctrine of Divine Decrees: Definition and Overview
text: The decree of God is His eternal, holy, wise, and sovereign purpose, comprehending at once all things that ever were or will be — their causes, conditions, successions, and relations — and determining their certain future. This definition has several critical components.

section: II. The Doctrine of Divine Decrees: Definition and Overview
text: First, the decree is eternal: it was formed in eternity past, not in time. God never learns, never revises, never supplements His knowledge. What He knows at any moment He has always known. There never was a time when He did not know everything that would ever occur.

section: II. The Doctrine of Divine Decrees: Definition and Overview
text: Second, the decree is holy and wise: it is compatible with the divine essence in every attribute. God cannot contradict His own nature. The essence and attributes of God necessitated His willing the highest and the best for mankind.

section: II. The Doctrine of Divine Decrees: Definition and Overview
text: Third, the decree is sovereign: it originates entirely within the will of God. It is not shaped by external pressure, creature input, or contingent events. It is not reactive but originative.

section: II. The Doctrine of Divine Decrees: Definition and Overview
text: Fourth, the decree is comprehensive: it encompasses all things, including the minutiae of sparrows falling and hairs dropping from a human head. Not the slightest uncertainty could exist as to even one of the smallest events without introducing confusion into all events, since all events are interwoven and interdependent.

section: III. The Mechanics of the Divine Decrees
text: III. The Mechanics of the Divine Decrees

section: III. The Mechanics of the Divine Decrees
text: Point two in the doctrine of divine decrees concerns the mechanical function of the divine plan. Three mechanics are operative: omniscience feeding the computer, the computer itself (the decrees), and the printout (election, foreknowledge, and predestination applying to believers).

section: First Mechanic: Omniscience
text: First Mechanic: Omniscience

section: First Mechanic: Omniscience
text: The omniscience of God knows perfectly, eternally, and simultaneously all that is knowable — both actual and possible. Such knowledge is totally compatible with the divine essence. God is eternal; His knowledge is eternal. God is sovereign; His knowledge is infinitely superior to any creature knowledge or creature intellect.

section: First Mechanic: Omniscience
text: Every minute detail of both angelic and human creation is completely and perfectly known in the divine mind at all times. There never was a time when God did not know every thought, every decision, every act that would ever occur. Omniscience perceives the free as free and the necessary as necessary, together with all their causes, conditions, and relations, as one indivisible system — every link of which is essential to the integrity of the whole.

section: First Mechanic: Omniscience
text: Time has no bearing on divine knowledge. The future is as perspicuous to God as the past. Omniscience also encompasses the alternatives to everything that could have happened but did not: the decisions not made, the actions not taken, the paths not followed. God knows all that would have been involved in every case where a creature's decision might have been different from what it actually was.

section: First Mechanic: Omniscience
text: Three categories of divine knowledge are distinguishable. First, divine self-knowledge: God's perfect knowledge of His own essence, the Trinity, and everything pertaining to the members of the Godhead. Second, omniscience proper: knowledge of everything pertaining to history, creation, time, and space — including the actual and the possible. Third, foreknowledge: a more limited category that must be carefully distinguished from omniscience.

section: Second Mechanic: The Computer of Divine Decrees
text: Second Mechanic: The Computer of Divine Decrees

section: Second Mechanic: The Computer of Divine Decrees
text: The omniscience of God feeds only facts into the computer of divine decrees. This was accomplished simultaneously in eternity past — not by stages, not sequentially in time. Every thought, every decision, every action of every creature was entered into the decrees. The decrees then became the complete and consummated purpose of God's sovereignty, determining the certain future of all things in human history.

section: Second Mechanic: The Computer of Divine Decrees
text: No event is directly caused by the decrees. The decree provides in every case that events shall be affected by their causes, acting in a manner consistent with the nature of those events. God does not override self-determination. He does not alter the tape. The free agent remains genuinely free. In the case of every free will act of a moral agent, the decree provides: (a) that the agent shall be a free agent; (b) that his antecedents and all antecedents of every act in question shall be what they are; (c) that all present conditions of the act shall be what they are; (d) that the act shall be perfectly spontaneous and free on the part of the agent; and (e) that it shall be certainly future.

section: Second Mechanic: The Computer of Divine Decrees
text: The decrees, vested solely in the will of God, determined what creation would be. This determination does not eliminate creaturely freedom but incorporates it. God knew billions of years before any decision was made exactly how self-determination would operate in every case — and that foreknowledge coexists perfectly with genuine freedom.

section: Third Mechanic: The Printout — Election, Foreknowledge, Predestination
text: Third Mechanic: The Printout — Election, Foreknowledge, Predestination

section: Third Mechanic: The Printout — Election, Foreknowledge, Predestination
text: The printout from the computer of divine decrees applies to believers only. It has three components: election, foreknowledge, and predestination (also called foreordination or predetermination). These three are not synonyms but distinct aspects of one integrated divine purpose.

section: Third Mechanic: The Printout — Election, Foreknowledge, Predestination
text: Predetermination — foreordination — is an act of the infinite and eternal omniscience of God determining the certain future of all events related to the believer. It never applies to unbelievers. The decree or foreordination alone establishes certainty. Nothing can be foreknown until it has first been decreed. The foreknowledge of God makes nothing certain; it merely perceives what is already certain through the decrees.

section: Third Mechanic: The Printout — Election, Foreknowledge, Predestination
text: Foreknowledge is not the same as omniscience. Omniscience includes knowledge of the actual and the possible. Foreknowledge deals with the actual only — specifically, with what is within the plan of God as it pertains to believers. Being omniscient, God knows all that would have been involved had He adopted any one of an infinite number of alternative plans, as well as the consequences had man chosen differently. Foreknowledge is the printout from the computer; it does not feed the computer. Logically: omniscience feeds into the decrees; foreknowledge reads out from them.

section: Third Mechanic: The Printout — Election, Foreknowledge, Predestination
text: Election is the plan of God for believers only. It is the key to understanding the Jewish problem related to the Abrahamic, Palestinian, Davidic, and New Covenants. The gracious and unconditional promises contained in those covenants can only be fulfilled to the elect — that is, to those who have believed in Christ and received the imputation of divine righteousness and eternal life. Colossians 3:15 identifies the supergrace blessings of maturity as themselves the content of election: 'You have been elected into one body' — the body that receives imputed blessing.

section: IV. The Origin of the Jewish Race and the Principle of Spiritual Election
text: IV. The Origin of the Jewish Race and the Principle of Spiritual Election

section: IV. The Origin of the Jewish Race and the Principle of Spiritual Election
text: The doctrine of divine decrees illuminates the origin of the Jewish race and resolves the apparent problem of divine favoritism that Paul addresses in Romans 9. All Gentile peoples descend from Noah through Shem, Ham, and Japheth and are formed through ordinary physical birth. The Jewish race is unique: it was formed not through ordinary generation but through a spiritually conditioned event. When Abraham was approximately one hundred years old — having already been a mature believer — his physical capacity to father a child was restored by divine action. The fourth race in human history was therefore formed in connection with maturity adjustment to the justice of God.

section: IV. The Origin of the Jewish Race and the Principle of Spiritual Election
text: The omniscience of God fed the actual facts into the computer of divine decrees. Abraham's brother Nahor remained an unbeliever — that was his own decision, the result of his own free will. Abraham became a believer and eventually a mature believer — that was his own decision. The printout for Abraham is election; the printout for Nahor is condemnation. God caused neither outcome. Both were the product of genuine self-determination, known in advance by omniscience and incorporated into the decrees.

section: IV. The Origin of the Jewish Race and the Principle of Spiritual Election
text: The same pattern repeats in the next generation. Ishmael was fed into the computer as an unbeliever — his own decision. Isaac was fed in as a believer — his own decision. In the following generation, Jacob was fed in as a believer and Esau as an unbeliever — again, by their own free determination. The printout of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob constitutes the foundation of the Jewish race. Election, in this context, is election of a race whose very origin lies in regeneration, not in physical descent.

section: IV. The Origin of the Jewish Race and the Principle of Spiritual Election
text: This is the great and tragic irony that Paul addresses in Romans 9: the racial Jews possess the genes of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, but they do not thereby automatically possess the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. The God of Israel is the Lord Jesus Christ — the Shekinah glory who was invisible to Israel throughout the Old Testament period and visibly present during His earthly ministry. The Shekinah glory became flesh and tabernacled among His people. To be the physical seed of Abraham and not the spiritual seed of Abraham — to carry the genetic heritage without the regenerate reality — is the greatest tragedy of human history.

section: IV. The Origin of the Jewish Race and the Principle of Spiritual Election
text: The Lord Jesus Christ Himself addressed this directly in His conversation with Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews who came to Him by night (John 3). Nicodemus held the genes of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; he was a Pharisee of highest rank. Yet the Shekinah glory told him, 'You must be born again.' Nicodemus misunderstood, thinking of physical birth. The Lord clarified: the second birth is spiritual, not physical. The second birth is what makes one a true Jew. All who are physical Israel are not thereby spiritual Israel. All Israel is not Israel. This is precisely the thesis of Romans 9:6.

section: IV. The Origin of the Jewish Race and the Principle of Spiritual Election
text: The promises of the Abrahamic, Palestinian, Davidic, and New Covenants are forever promises: a land forever, a people forever, a king forever, a covenant forever. These forever promises require forever life in their recipients. Human life imputed to the soul at physical birth is not sufficient. Eternal life imputed to the human spirit at regeneration is the prerequisite for inheriting forever promises. The justice of God simultaneously creates the human spirit through the agency of God the Holy Spirit and imputes eternal life to that spirit at the moment of faith in Christ. Righteousness is then imputed on the basis of that faith. Blessing in time and blessing in eternity both flow from imputed righteousness — and imputed righteousness comes only through faith in Christ. There is no alternative route.

section: IV. The Origin of the Jewish Race and the Principle of Spiritual Election
text: 2 Corinthians 9:10–11 captures the logic: 'Now He who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your seed for sowing and increase the harvest of your righteousness. You will be enriched in everything for all liberality, which through us is producing thanksgiving to God.' The harvest of Israel must be imputed righteousness, not righteousness produced by law-keeping. Righteousness produced by works is human righteousness — insufficient, negative. The righteousness required is divine righteousness imputed by faith — the only basis on which the forever promises can be fulfilled.

section: V. Characteristics of the Divine Decrees
text: V. Characteristics of the Divine Decrees

section: V. Characteristics of the Divine Decrees
text: The fourth point in the doctrine of divine decrees concerns the characteristics of the decrees themselves. These characteristics are essential for answering the charge of divine unrighteousness raised in Romans 9:14.

section: V. Characteristics of the Divine Decrees
text: First, the decrees include all the facts of history — facts which are fed into the divine computer by the omniscience of God. There is one all-inclusive will and purpose of God concerning all that ever was or will be. This will and purpose originated entirely within God Himself, compatible with His essence and related to His eternal glory. The decrees reach all the way down to the minutiae of creaturely life — even the fall of a sparrow, even the count of hairs on a human head.

section: V. Characteristics of the Divine Decrees
text: Second, the members of the Trinity function in the decrees in a manner that is immanent, intrinsic, and perfectly subjective. Divine subjectivity is perfect; human subjectivity is always imperfect. The Father sends the Son; the Father and Son send the Spirit. How God supports and sustains the believer is extrinsic, transient, and objective — the outward expression of the inward perfection of the divine plan.

section: V. Characteristics of the Divine Decrees
text: Third, the decrees are efficacious: they certainly determine all that ever was or ever will be. The foreknowledge of God makes nothing certain; it merely perceives what is already certain through the decrees. The decrees make all things certain.

section: V. Characteristics of the Divine Decrees
text: Fourth, the decrees are all-comprehensive. Not the slightest uncertainty could exist as to even one of the smallest events without introducing confusion into all events. All events are interwoven and interdependent — including prayer. Prayer is not squeezed out by the decrees; it is incorporated within them. Philippians 4:6 commands: 'Stop worrying about anything; in everything by prayer and supplication, after thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.' Colossians 4:2 reinforces: 'Devote yourselves to prayer, being watchful in it with thanksgiving.' Prayer is a decreed instrumentality.

section: V. Characteristics of the Divine Decrees
text: Fifth, the decrees are eternal. God never gains knowledge. What He knows at any time He has always known. The decrees were decreed simultaneously in eternity past, not sequentially or in stages.

section: V. Characteristics of the Divine Decrees
text: Sixth, the decrees are perfect. God is perfect; therefore His plan is perfect. The only imperfect element is man within the plan. A perfect God produces a perfect plan for imperfect persons. The plan maintains its perfection and integrity through a policy of grace. God never loses His perfection; His plan never fails, even when man fails. Grace accommodates failure without compromising the integrity of the plan.

section: V. Characteristics of the Divine Decrees
text: Seventh, the decrees are unchangeable and certain. Nothing will ever arise to necessitate a change. Everything was known, decreed, and made certain in eternity past. God is bound not by external constraint but by His own infinite faithfulness, incorruptible integrity, and immutable truth to complete what He has decreed. God plays out the entire tape — He does not fast-forward past sin, human good, or evil. Every decision a creature makes, however catastrophic, was incorporated into the decree.

section: V. Characteristics of the Divine Decrees
text: Eighth, God has decreed ends as well as means, causes as well as effects, conditions and instrumentalities as well as the events that depend on them. Some things God has decreed to accomplish directly — creation, salvation, the control of history. Other things God accomplishes through secondary causes. Still others God has decreed to permit free agents to do through the exercise of their own self-determination, even including the operation of the old sin nature in sin, human good, and evil. Yet whether accomplished through primary, secondary, or tertiary causes, the decree is equally binding and certain in every category.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Eighty-Three
text: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Eighty-Three

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Eighty-Three
text: 1. Thanksgiving is a function of doctrine, not of circumstance. The mature believer gives thanks not because conditions are favorable but because Bible doctrine resident in the right lobe produces a capacity that transcends circumstance. Logistical grace provides the baseline — food, shelter, the opportunity to hear the Word — but mature thanksgiving is motivated by the imputation of supergrace blessing at the maturity barrier. Without doctrine, thanksgiving is superficial human gratitude. With maximum doctrine in the soul, it overflows as a sacrificial offering of the royal priest.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Eighty-Three
text: 2. The divine decrees are the framework within which Romans 9:14 must be interpreted. The charge that God is unrighteous in hating Esau or hardening Pharaoh arises from a misunderstanding of the relationship between omniscience, decree, foreknowledge, and election. Once the mechanics are understood — omniscience feeding actual facts into the decree, the decree establishing certainty, foreknowledge reading out the result for believers only — the charge collapses. God does not predetermine unbelief; He incorporates the actual decisions of free agents into a comprehensive and just plan.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Eighty-Three
text: 3. Election, foreknowledge, and predestination apply to believers only. These three terms describe the printout from the computer of divine decrees as it pertains exclusively to those who believe in Christ. Predestination never applies to unbelievers. The condemnation of Nahor, Ishmael, and Esau is not the product of divine predestination but of their own negative volition, which the omniscience of God incorporated into the decree without causing it.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Eighty-Three
text: 4. The Jewish race was formed through regeneration, not physical generation. The origin of the Jewish race in Abraham's believing faith — followed by Isaac's and Jacob's — establishes the irreducible principle that Israel is constituted spiritually, not biologically. The forever promises of the Abrahamic, Palestinian, Davidic, and New Covenants can only be fulfilled to those who possess forever life. Physical descent from Abraham without regeneration leaves a Jew outside the covenant promises and outside the elect nation that will inherit them.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Eighty-Three
text: 5. The decrees are all-comprehensive, incorporating prayer as a decreed instrumentality. The comprehensiveness of the divine decrees does not eliminate prayer but includes it. Prayer is a means decreed by God through which certain ends are accomplished. The commands of Philippians 4:6 and Colossians 4:2 — both associating prayer with thanksgiving — stand within the decree, not outside it. Believers are commanded to pray because prayer is part of the divine plan, not despite the decree but as an expression of it.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Eighty-Three
text: 6. The perfection of the divine plan is maintained through grace, not through the elimination of failure. God's plan is perfect even though man is imperfect. The plan incorporates sin, human good, and evil without being compromised by them, because grace provides the mechanism by which God can deal with imperfect creatures while maintaining His perfect integrity. The decrees are unchangeable not because nothing goes wrong but because God knew in eternity past everything that would go wrong and incorporated every failure into a plan that remains perfectly righteous throughout.

section: Romans 9:13 — Divine Decrees, Omniscience, and the Blessing of Man
text: Romans 9:13 — Divine Decrees, Omniscience, and the Blessing of Man

section: Romans 9:13 — Divine Decrees, Omniscience, and the Blessing of Man
text: Romans 9:13 “As it is written, 'Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated.'” (ESV)

section: Romans 9:13 — Divine Decrees, Omniscience, and the Blessing of Man
text: Corrected translation: Just as it is written: Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated.

section: Romans 9:13 — Divine Decrees, Omniscience, and the Blessing of Man
text: This chapter continues the preparatory doctrinal groundwork for Paul's exegesis of Romans 9:13 — the divine hatred of Esau and the hardening of Pharaoh's heart. Before those passages can be rightly interpreted, the doctrine of divine decrees must be thoroughly understood. What does it mean that God knew every thought, every decision, and every action of every creature before history began? How do election, foreknowledge, and predestination function within the decree structure? And how does the imputation of divine blessing — not human works — constitute the organizing principle of God's plan? These questions are addressed in the extended doctrinal treatment that follows.

section: I. The Will of God and the Divine Decrees
text: I. The Will of God and the Divine Decrees

section: I. The Will of God and the Divine Decrees
text: The doctrine of divine decrees has been under study for several sessions. Having examined its definition, its mechanics, and its characteristics, we turn now to the relationship between the will of God and the decrees.

section: A. Unity and Scope of the Divine Will
text: A. Unity and Scope of the Divine Will

section: A. Unity and Scope of the Divine Will
text: There is one all-inclusive will and purpose of God concerning all that ever was or ever will be, from the beginning of human history through the last day of the Millennium. Because God knew every thought, every action, and every decision that has ever occurred or ever will occur, all of it resides within one comprehensive decree. Many things are printed out of that computer, but they are all contained within it from the outset.

section: A. Unity and Scope of the Divine Will
text: This will and purpose of God originates from within Himself — long before any creature of any category ever existed, whether angelic or human. It is therefore designed entirely for the glory, pleasure, and satisfaction of God. All creatures have been placed into space and time, and all events related to space and time were simultaneously decreed.

section: A. Unity and Scope of the Divine Will
text: These events resolved themselves in divine action in two categories. First, divine action within the Godhead — the actions of the members of the Trinity — which are immanent, intrinsic, and subjective in the proper sense. Second, actions related to creation, which are extrinsic (taking cognizance of angelic and human volition), transient (chronological in their execution), and objective. This second category constitutes the function of divine justice as the point of reference for the human race.

section: B. The Formation of the Jewish Race
text: B. The Formation of the Jewish Race

section: B. The Formation of the Jewish Race
text: From the Gentile races descending from Noah through Shem, Ham, and Japheth, God formed the unique Jewish race so that He might have a client nation — a priest nation — in the Dispensation of Israel. The omniscience of God knew, before history began, every decision every person would ever make, and only facts were fed into the computer of divine decrees.

section: B. The Formation of the Jewish Race
text: Abraham was by birth a Gentile of the Semitic branch. At approximately age 100 he became the first Jew — this was inseparable from his maturity adjustment to the justice of God and the resulting imputation of divine blessing from the justice of God to the righteousness of God resident in him. His older brother Nahor remained a Gentile, maintaining a posture of negative volition throughout his life and never departing from the Gentile racial category. Accordingly, Abraham's printout from the computer of divine decrees reads: election, foreknowledge, predestination. Nahor's printout reads: condemnation. These are entirely distinct categories.

section: B. The Formation of the Jewish Race
text: The terms foreknowledge, election, and predestination are never used in Scripture for the unbeliever. They are printouts for the believer only. God's omniscience knew billions of years ago that Isaac would believe and eventually crack the maturity barrier, distinguishing him from his half-brother Ishmael, who remained negative and whose printout is condemnation. Isaac remained in the line of the Jewish race, and at the moment of faith the righteousness of God was imputed to him — establishing the target for all subsequent divine blessing. The same is true for Jacob, the believing twin, whose printout reads election; and Esau, the unbelieving twin, whose printout reads condemnation. These are the individuals at the center of Romans 9:13.

section: B. The Formation of the Jewish Race
text: No Jew is truly a Jew in the deepest sense until he believes in the Lord Jesus Christ and is born again. The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob is the Lord Jesus Christ — the Shekinah glory. This is the origin of the Jewish race and the key to understanding its historical problems.

section: C. Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience and the Decrees
text: C. Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience and the Decrees

section: C. Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience and the Decrees
text: Three types of divine knowledge must be carefully distinguished: self-knowledge, omniscience, and foreknowledge. They are not synonymous and must not be conflated.

section: C. Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience and the Decrees
text: Self-knowledge — God's eternal knowledge of Himself and the other members of the Trinity, who are co-equal and co-eternal in essence while distinct in personality.

section: C. Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience and the Decrees
text: Omniscience — God's knowledge of all actual and potential facts in all of history. Omniscience feeds only actual facts — not wishes, not possibilities apart from reality — into the computer of divine decrees.

section: C. Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience and the Decrees
text: Foreknowledge — not the source of the decrees, but a printout from the computer. Foreknowledge makes nothing certain. It merely perceives and acknowledges what is already decreed. Nothing can be foreknown until it was first decreed. Foreknowledge is cognizance of what is decreed.

section: C. Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience and the Decrees
text: This sequence is logically precise: omniscience feeds information into the computer; the decrees are the all-inclusive plan; foreknowledge acknowledges what the decrees contain. Conflating omniscience with foreknowledge produces theological confusion and leads to misreadings of passages such as Romans 8:29 and 9:13.

section: II. Characteristics and Synonyms of the Divine Decrees
text: II. Characteristics and Synonyms of the Divine Decrees

section: II. Characteristics and Synonyms of the Divine Decrees
text: Several further characteristics of the divine decrees require careful definition before the doctrinal application can be made.

section: II. Characteristics and Synonyms of the Divine Decrees
text: The decrees are efficacious, determining all that ever was or will be, including the directive, permissive, and overruling will of God. All things depend on God's will, and nothing is certain apart from His will. At the point where theology requires it, the will of God and the decrees must be understood as synonymous. Synonymous terms include: foreordination, predetermination, the decrees, and the sovereign will of God.

section: II. Characteristics and Synonyms of the Divine Decrees
text: The decrees originate from God's omniscience in eternity past, separating fact from fiction. Therefore a clear distinction must be maintained between the omniscience of God and the foreknowledge of God: the former feeds facts into the computer; the latter reads out what is already there. Nothing can be foreknown until it was first decreed. Accordingly, the decrees — not foreknowledge — are what make events certain.

section: II. Characteristics and Synonyms of the Divine Decrees
text: A further distinction must be made between the decrees of God and the desires of God. The decrees contain all the facts of history — every sin, every act of human good, every act of evil — because they record the actual exercise of human and angelic free will. Many of those facts are contrary to what God desires. God desires that every person be saved; yet the person who says no at God-consciousness and no at gospel hearing is decreed accordingly. The decrees contain both what pleases God and what violates His desires — but both are included under one all-comprehensive plan.

section: II. Characteristics and Synonyms of the Divine Decrees
text: Sin, human good, and evil are not the desires of God, but they are in the decrees because people sin, perform human good, and commit evil from their own free will. God did not desire the consignment of conscious creatures to the lake of fire forever, but it is decreed under the printout of retribution for all who express negative volition at God-consciousness and at gospel hearing. Similarly, God does not desire the discipline of believers, but divine discipline is decreed for all carnality and reversionism, because human beings are responsible for their own decisions as free agents.

section: II. Characteristics and Synonyms of the Divine Decrees
text: A final distinction must be made between the decrees of God in eternity past and God's actions in time. The action of God in time is the execution of the decrees established in eternity past. The execution is not the decree, but logically follows it. This also requires a distinction between God's decrees and God's laws: the decrees constitute the plan and action of God, while God's laws regulate human conduct in space and time. The laws of God are completely revealed in Scripture, while the decrees are only partially revealed in eschatological passages.

section: II. Characteristics and Synonyms of the Divine Decrees
text: God did not decree Himself to be. God eternally existed before and outside of the divine decrees, so that the divine decrees do not act upon God, but God acts upon the decrees.

section: III. The Divine Decrees and the Blessing of Man
text: III. The Divine Decrees and the Blessing of Man

section: III. The Divine Decrees and the Blessing of Man
text: The relationship between the divine decrees and the blessing of man is organized around seven imputations that together constitute the plan of God. These imputations are the structural backbone of everything Paul is arguing in Romans 9.

section: A. The Seven Imputations
text: A. The Seven Imputations

section: A. The Seven Imputations
text: Five of the seven imputations are real imputations — meaning they have an antecedent home, a natural target to which the imputed element belongs. Two are judicial imputations, meaning they have no natural antecedent target; they are acts of the justice of God in which something is placed where it does not naturally reside.

section: A. The Seven Imputations
text: The plan is organized into three categories, which we may designate as the X, Y, and Z equations.

section: B. The X Equation: Birth to Regeneration
text: B. The X Equation: Birth to Regeneration

section: B. The X Equation: Birth to Regeneration
text: Imputation 1 — Human life imputed to the soul at birth. There is no life in the womb in the Biblical sense; there is reflex motility, but not the divinely imputed human life. At birth, God imputes human life to the human soul, and that life is permanent. No sin, no deed, no action can ever separate human life from the soul. Those who never reach God-consciousness — due to mental incapacity or death in infancy — are automatically saved, because their volition is not implicated in the angelic conflict.

section: B. The X Equation: Birth to Regeneration
text: Imputation 2 — Adam's original sin imputed to the old sin nature. This is a real imputation: Adam's original sin has a genetically formed home — the old sin nature (OSN) — transmitted through the male line. This imputation occurs simultaneously with the imputation of human life, producing immediate condemnation. Condemnation must precede salvation. This arrangement also ensures that personal sins are reserved for a later, judicial imputation at the cross. No one is ever condemned on the basis of his first personal sin — only Adam was. The second imputation creates the first potential: the potential for salvation.

section: B. The X Equation: Birth to Regeneration
text: The X equation therefore reads: human life imputed at birth, plus Adam's original sin imputed to the old sin nature, equals the first potential — salvation through faith in Christ. The pertinent doctrine of the gospel, when received, produces the first hope: absolute confidence that faith in Christ means eternal salvation. When that faith is exercised, the hope becomes reality — eternal salvation.

section: C. The Y Equation: Salvation and the Imputation of Righteousness
text: C. The Y Equation: Salvation and the Imputation of Righteousness

section: C. The Y Equation: Salvation and the Imputation of Righteousness
text: Judicial Imputation 1 — All personal sins imputed to Christ on the cross. At the cross, every personal sin of every human being who would ever live was imputed to the Lord Jesus Christ and judged. This is the basis of salvation.

section: C. The Y Equation: Salvation and the Imputation of Righteousness
text: Judicial Imputation 2 — Divine righteousness imputed to the believer at salvation. This is a judicial imputation because it has no natural antecedent: the sinner has no home for God's righteousness. But once imputed, that righteousness becomes the target — the potential home — for all subsequent divine blessing. Justice demands that God impute blessing only to His own righteousness resident in the believer. This is why no amount of human works, talent, or merit can ever obtain one unit of divine blessing. The second imputation creates the second potential: blessing.

section: C. The Y Equation: Salvation and the Imputation of Righteousness
text: Imputation 3 — Eternal life imputed to the human spirit. God the Holy Spirit simultaneously creates a human spirit at salvation — this is regeneration, being born again. Eternal life is then imputed as a real imputation to that newly created human spirit. It is permanent. No sin, no action, no reversionism can ever remove eternal life from the human spirit. This is the basis of eternal security.

section: C. The Y Equation: Salvation and the Imputation of Righteousness
text: The Y equation: judicial imputation of all personal sins to Christ, plus judicial imputation of divine righteousness to the believer, equals the second potential — blessing in time. The pertinent doctrine of the Christian life, consistently learned and applied, produces the second hope: absolute confidence that maturity adjustment to the justice of God will result in the imputation of divine blessing. When the maturity barrier is cracked through maximum doctrine resident in the soul, that hope becomes reality.

section: D. The Z Equation: Maturity, Blessing, and Eternal Glory
text: D. The Z Equation: Maturity, Blessing, and Eternal Glory

section: D. The Z Equation: Maturity, Blessing, and Eternal Glory
text: The Z equation takes cognizance of the two imputations from the Y equation as its foundation: eternal life at salvation (first plus) and blessing in time (second plus). The imputation of blessing in time is the potential for the imputation of blessing in eternity. If no blessing is imputed in time, there is no basis for eternal blessing at the judgment seat of Christ.

section: D. The Z Equation: Maturity, Blessing, and Eternal Glory
text: The logical structure here is the argument from the greater to the lesser — what Romans 5 establishes as the a fortiori principle. If the justice of God can impute the greater blessing — temporal blessing to divine righteousness at the point of maturity — it certainly follows that the justice of God can impute the lesser: eternal blessing to the resurrection body at the judgment seat of Christ. The imputation of eternal blessing at the judgment seat is secured precisely because blessing in time was first imputed.

section: D. The Z Equation: Maturity, Blessing, and Eternal Glory
text: This is the complete plan of God as structured through the seven imputations. It explains in systematic form what election, foreknowledge, and predestination mean for the believer — and why those terms are never applied to the unbeliever. It also explains the story of the Jewish race in Romans 9: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob received the righteousness of God at the moment of faith, establishing them as the bearers of the covenant promises. Their unbelieving counterparts — Nahor, Ishmael, Esau — received no such imputation and remain in the printout of condemnation.

section: E. Summary Principles
text: E. Summary Principles

section: E. Summary Principles
text: The omniscience of God, taking cognizance of the fall of mankind in the garden, graciously provided a plan based on imputations from divine justice. This plan involves seven imputations feeding maximum blessing to mankind in time and in eternity.

section: E. Summary Principles
text: Non-meritorious human volition can fall short of any potential within God's plan. To what extent every human being advances in this plan was known to the omniscience of God in eternity past and fed into the computer of divine decrees as fact. In too many cases the potential exceeds the reality. But only the reality was decreed — because only facts are fed into the computer.

section: E. Summary Principles
text: From this emerges the governing principle: the attainment of divine blessing through imputation is the means God has chosen to glorify Himself and to give Himself pleasure. The imputation of divine blessing to the mature believer emphasizes His grace and excludes human talent and human works. Blessing flows exclusively from the priesthood side — doctrine received, believed, and applied — never from production, witnessing, giving, or any other function of the ambassadorship.

section: IV. The Decrees and the Glory of God
text: IV. The Decrees and the Glory of God

section: IV. The Decrees and the Glory of God
text: Every point in the doctrine of divine decrees converges on this: the decrees unite in one all-inclusive and final objective — the glory of God. This principle appears in Proverbs 16:4, Romans 11:36, Hebrews 2:10, and Revelation 4:11.

section: IV. The Decrees and the Glory of God
text: Before all creation, the decrees of God concerned no one but the members of the Trinity and their eternal glory. The Father, Son, and Holy Spirit possessed perfect, eternal, and infinite glory in eternity past and will possess it in eternity future. Nothing any creature does can promote or diminish that glory. A believer can glorify God — but cannot promote God's glory, which is already infinite. A believer's failure cannot reduce it.

section: IV. The Decrees and the Glory of God
text: This means that the plan of God moves forward independently of any individual's success or failure. If a believer fails, the plan keeps moving. Divine discipline follows the failure, but the plan itself is not interrupted. It began in glory and ends in glory. The believer who advances in doctrine participates in that glory; the believer in reversionism is left behind under discipline.

section: IV. The Decrees and the Glory of God
text: Since the manifestation of God's declarative glory also secures the highest blessing for His creatures, it is inevitable that the imputation of blessing to the mature believer will glorify God — emphasizing His grace and categorically excluding human talent and human works. The decrees include every detail of every creature's experience: every thought, every decision, every seemingly minute circumstance.

section: IV. The Decrees and the Glory of God
text: As the origin and subject of the divine decrees, God is glorified in everything that history produces — both the decisions that give Him pleasure and those that violate His desires. The believer in Supergrace A, Supergrace B, or Ultra-supergrace represents the highest positive expression of this glory in the human realm.

section: IV. The Decrees and the Glory of God
text: The decrees, though appearing many to the finite mind, are one plan to God — embracing both cause and effect, both means and end. God is glorified and pleased in the momentum and advance of believers within His plan. The omniscience of God knew in eternity past what thoughts, motivations, decisions, and actions would carry one believer to maturity and another into reversionism. God has prepared magnificent blessing by imputation for the mature believer, and He has prepared concentrated divine discipline for the believer in reversionism. Since there is no lake of fire and no eternal suffering for the believer, all discipline is concentrated in time.

section: V. The Decrees and Human Freedom
text: V. The Decrees and Human Freedom

section: V. The Decrees and Human Freedom
text: The plan of God and the decrees of God are entirely consistent with human freedom and volition. God does not limit, coerce, or violate human self-determination. This is a categorical statement that must be understood before Paul's argument in Romans 9 can be followed.

section: V. The Decrees and Human Freedom
text: A distinction must be maintained between what God causes directly — such as the cross — and what God permits indirectly — such as sin, human good, and evil. God created man with free will, that is, volition resident in the soul. He therefore permits human volition to function in self-determination. Without that permission, there would have been no fall of man. The permissive will is just as much a part of the decrees, and therefore just as glorifying to God, as the directive will.

section: V. The Decrees and Human Freedom
text: God is not the author of sin or human evil in any form. Free will and self-determination are the origin and source of sin, human good, and evil. Both sin and the cross are fed into the computer of divine decrees by the omniscience of God — one as the direct will of God, the other as the permissive will. The divine decrees are simply the facts of human history in the mind of God in eternity past.

section: V. The Decrees and Human Freedom
text: Since the decrees are the sum total of God's plan and indicate His purpose designed in eternity past, they inevitably center around the unique person of the Lord Jesus Christ. It is at the cross that the sovereignty of God met the free will of man — for the glory of God and the momentum of the plan of God. Under the divine policy of grace, the work of salvation is accomplished by God; man benefits entirely apart from his own human merit or works.

section: V. The Decrees and Human Freedom
text: God's plan was so designed in eternity past as to include all events and all actions related to their causes and conditions as parts of one indivisible system, every link being part of the integrity of the whole. This is why all things work together for good (Romans 8:28). Without violating human volition, God has provided a plan so perfect that it includes directive provision, preservation, function, cause and effect for all believers.

section: V. The Decrees and Human Freedom
text: God has decreed to accomplish some things directly, some through secondary agencies such as Israel and the Church, and some through individuals such as the Apostle Paul. Primary, secondary, and tertiary functions all constitute one all-comprehensive plan — perfect, eternal, unchangeable, and without any compromise of divine integrity. The only revelation of the divine decrees is found in the content of the Bible. This is why the perception of doctrine is the highest priority of the Christian life and the only adequate preparation for historical pressure.

section: V. The Decrees and Human Freedom
text: All of this doctrinal framework — the structure of the decrees, the three types of divine knowledge, the seven imputations, the relationship between the will of God and human self-determination — is the necessary preparation for the exegesis of Romans 9:13: “Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated.” That passage will be addressed in the following chapter.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Eighty-Four
text: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Eighty-Four

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Eighty-Four
text: 1. Three types of divine knowledge must be distinguished: self-knowledge, omniscience, and foreknowledge. Omniscience feeds only actual facts into the computer of divine decrees. Foreknowledge is a printout of what is already decreed — it makes nothing certain. Only the decrees make events certain.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Eighty-Four
text: 2. The decrees of God are the facts of all human history in the mind of God in eternity past. They precede history entirely. They contain everything that every creature would ever think, decide, or do — including sin, human good, and evil — without God being the author of any of them.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Eighty-Four
text: 3. The decrees and the will of God are synonymous with foreordination, predetermination, and the sovereign will of God: these are not competing concepts but synonymous terms for the one all-inclusive plan. Directive, permissive, and overruling will are all contained within the decrees.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Eighty-Four
text: 4. Foreknowledge, election, and predestination are printout terms for believers only. They are never applied to unbelievers in Scripture. The unbeliever's printout is condemnation, reprobation, and judgment — the result of negative volition at God-consciousness and at gospel hearing, which the omniscience of God knew in eternity past and fed into the computer as fact.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Eighty-Four
text: 5. The plan of God is organized around seven imputations. Five are real imputations (having natural antecedent homes); two are judicial imputations (having no natural antecedent). The second imputation in each equation establishes the potential: condemnation creates the potential for salvation; divine righteousness creates the potential for blessing; blessing in time creates the potential for eternal blessing.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Eighty-Four
text: 6. Divine blessing is imputed exclusively from the justice of God to the righteousness of God resident in the mature believer. No human work, production, witnessing, giving, or talent contributes one unit of blessing. Blessing flows entirely from the priesthood side through the intake and application of Bible doctrine. Works are the result of advance, never its cause.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Eighty-Four
text: 7. The decrees are fully consistent with human freedom. God does not coerce, limit, or violate human self-determination. The fall of man was permitted, not caused. The unbeliever's rejection of Christ is decreed as fact — not as God's desire, but as the exercise of free will, which the omniscience of God incorporated into the decrees in eternity past.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Eighty-Four
text: 8. God's glory is infinite, eternal, and independent of any creature. God possessed perfect glory in eternity past and will possess it in eternity future. No creature promotes or diminishes it. The believer glorifies God by advancing to maturity and receiving the imputation of divine blessing — not by human production. The plan of God moves forward with or without any individual's participation.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Eighty-Four
text: 9. The doctrine of divine decrees is not abstract theology — it is essential preparation for historical pressure. The believer who understands how the decrees function, how divine blessing is imputed, and how human volition relates to God's plan will be able to apply doctrine under personal disaster, collective pressure, and historical crisis. The believer in reversionism, lacking this framework, will panic, accuse God of injustice, and fail.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Five Hundred Eighty-Four
text: 10. The only revelation of the divine decrees is found in Scripture. Therefore, consistent, systematic perception of Bible doctrine is the highest priority of the Christian life. It is the sole means of advancing through the X, Y, and Z equations of the plan of God and the only adequate preparation for the coming exegesis of Romans 9:13.

section: Glossary
text: Divine decrees

section: Glossary
text: The all-inclusive, eternal, sovereign purpose of God comprehending at once all things that ever were or will be — every thought, decision, and action of every creature — in their causes, conditions, successions, and relations, determining their certain future occurrence. The decrees are the facts of all human history in the mind of God in eternity past.

section: Glossary
text: Omniscience

section: Glossary
text: One of the three categories of divine knowledge. God's knowledge of all actual and potential facts in all of history. Omniscience feeds only actual facts into the computer of divine decrees. It is distinguished from self-knowledge (God's eternal knowledge of Himself) and from foreknowledge (a printout of what is already decreed).

section: Glossary
text: Foreknowledge

section: Glossary
text: πρόγνωσις prognōsis — foreknowledge

section: Glossary
text: Not the source or cause of the decrees, but a printout of what the omniscience of God fed into the computer of divine decrees. Foreknowledge makes nothing certain; it merely perceives and acknowledges what is already certain by decree. Nothing can be foreknown until it was first decreed.

section: Glossary
text: Election

section: Glossary
text: ἐκλογή eklogē — election, selection

section: Glossary
text: A printout term for the believer only. The divine selection of the believer, known in eternity past through the omniscience of God, based on the factual reality of that person's faith in Christ. Never applied to unbelievers in Scripture.

section: Glossary
text: Predestination

section: Glossary
text: προορίζω proorizō — to predetermine, to foreordain

section: Glossary
text: A printout term for the believer only. The divine foreordination of all that the believer will become and receive in Christ — including election, adoption, and ultimate glorification. Synonymous with foreordination and predetermination as applied to the plan of God.

section: Glossary
text: Real imputation

section: Glossary
text: An imputation in which the thing imputed has a natural antecedent home — a target for which there is an affinity. Five of the seven imputations in God's plan are real imputations: human life to the soul, Adam's original sin to the old sin nature, eternal life to the human spirit, blessing in time to divine righteousness, and blessing in eternity to the resurrection body.

section: Glossary
text: Judicial imputation

section: Glossary
text: An imputation in which the thing imputed has no natural antecedent home. Two of the seven imputations are judicial: all personal sins imputed to Christ on the cross, and divine righteousness imputed to the believing sinner at salvation. Both are acts of divine justice without natural affinity between the imputed element and its recipient.

section: Glossary
text: Old sin nature (OSN)

section: Glossary
text: The sin capacity inherited at birth through the male genetic line. The natural antecedent home for the imputation of Adam's original sin. The OSN is the source of personal sin, human good, and evil in the believer's experience throughout the Christian life.

section: Glossary
text: Maturity adjustment to the justice of God

section: Glossary
text: δικαιοσύνη θεοῦ dikaiosynē theou — righteousness of God

section: Glossary
text: The progressive stage of adjustment in which the believer, through sustained daily intake of Bible doctrine under the filling of the Holy Spirit, cracks the maturity barrier and becomes the target for the imputation of divine blessing in time. Distinguished from salvation adjustment (instantaneous, at faith in Christ) and rebound adjustment (instantaneous, repeated; restores fellowship per 1 John 1:9).

section: Glossary
text: Reversionism

section: Glossary
text: Retroactive spiritual regression — the believer's return to the thinking, values, and motivations of the old sin nature. The reversionistic believer falls short of every potential in the plan of God and becomes the object of concentrated divine discipline in time.

section: Glossary
text: Supergrace / Ultra-supergrace

section: Glossary
text: Stages of spiritual maturity beyond the maturity barrier. Supergrace A denotes the initial breakthrough of the maturity barrier through maximum doctrine resident in the soul. Supergrace B and ultra-supergrace represent continued advance to higher levels of blessing imputed in time, with corresponding eternal blessing at the judgment seat of Christ.

section: Glossary
text: A fortiori

section: Glossary
text: a fortiori — from the greater to the lesser

section: Glossary
text: A logical argument establishing that if God can accomplish the greater, He certainly can accomplish the lesser. Applied in Romans 5 and in the imputation framework: if the justice of God can impute temporal blessing to divine righteousness at maturity, it certainly follows that He can impute eternal blessing to the resurrection body at the judgment seat of Christ.

section: Glossary
text: Logistical grace

section: Glossary
text: God's provision of everything necessary for the believer's physical existence and continued function in the plan of God. Logistical grace is sustained by the justice of God and is independent of the believer's merit, works, or spiritual condition.

section: Glossary
text: Pivot

section: Glossary
text: The body of mature believers within a national entity whose adjustment to the justice of God sustains divine blessing on that nation. The pivot is the invisible spiritual infrastructure that determines a client nation's historical prosperity or discipline.
